q: The price component of oil is determined by using the monthly oil par price (PP) based on density.
b: The MRF Guidelines state that Alberta Energy determines a well's monthly revenue by 'multiplying volumes of all the hydrocarbons produced, including test production, by their respective par/reference prices as published in the Information Letters available on the Alberta Energy website' (Revenue = Production * Par Price), and that 'the price component of oil is determined by using the monthly oil par price (PP) based on density'. The rate brackets are literal par-price thresholds: PP <= 251.70, 251.70 < PP <= 409.02, 409.02 < PP <= 723.64, 723.64 < PP. The Petroleum Royalty Regulation, 2017 s.5 gives the Minister the power to 'determine an amount per cubic metre as the par price' for light, medium, heavy and ultra-heavy oil, and its Schedule sets rp% = [(par price - 251.70) x ...].
tt: Oil Par Prices
tp: Alberta Energy and Minerals / Alberta Petroleum Marketing Commission

q: the price component (rp) is the percentage rate based on the par/reference price for each hydrocarbon
b: Under MRF the post-C* royalty rate is rp% + rq%, where 'the price component (rp) is the percentage rate based on the par/reference price for each hydrocarbon'. C* is drawn down each month by revenue 'valued using the respective hydrocarbon par/reference price', and the gas rate tables in the guidelines are indexed on the monthly reference price in $/GJ. The Natural Gas Royalty Regulation, 2017 correspondingly requires the Minister to prescribe a Gas Reference Price 'for January, 2017 and for each subsequent' production month along with the methane, ethane, propane, butanes and pentanes plus ISC reference prices.
tt: Alberta Natural Gas Reference Price
tp: Alberta Energy and Minerals / Alberta Petroleum Marketing Commission

q: the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract of West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX
b: Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 (AR 223/2008) s.29 sets the gross royalty rate as RG% = 1% + [FG (A - B)], where FG is '8% divided by $65 per barrel', A is 'the lesser of the WTI price for the given month ... and $120 per barrel' and B is 'the lesser of A for the month and $55 per barrel'. s.29(3)(a) defines the monthly WTI price as 'the simple average of the WTI prices for the trading days of the preceding month, excluding any days where the trading price was at or below $0 per barrel', and s.29(4)(a) defines the daily WTI price as 'the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract of West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX'. The same A term drives the post-payout net royalty percentage factor, NRPF = 25% + (FN (A - B)).
tt: NYMEX Light Sweet Crude Oil (WTI) Futures Daily Settlement Prices

q: the actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rate for a day is that published in relation to that day by the Bank of Canada
b: Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 s.29(3) makes the Canadian-dollar WTI price 'the product of' the average US-dollar NYMEX settlement price and 'the simple average of the daily actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rates for that month'. s.29(4)(c) specifies that 'the actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rate for a day is that published in relation to that day by the Bank of Canada', and s.29(7) provides a substitution mechanism 'if the Bank of Canada no longer publishes' it.
tt: Bank of Canada Daily Exchange Rates

q: the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX
b: Bitumen Valuation Methodology (Ministerial) Regulation (AR 232/2008) s.1(3)(g) provides that 'the WTI price for a month shall be the simple average of the WTI prices for the trading days of the current month expressed in U.S. dollars', where a daily WTI price is 'the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX'. That WTI term enters the monthly Floor Price directly: Floor Price = greater of $10/m3 and MMSP - $250/m3 - A, where A is the greater of $0 and (BRENT - WTI).
tt: NYMEX Light Sweet Crude Oil (WTI) Futures Daily Settlement Prices

q: the simple average of the daily actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rates for the month published by the Bank of Canada, rounded to 5 decimal places
b: BVM (Ministerial) Regulation s.1(5) requires the Mexico Maya spot price, the Brent price, the WTI price, the synbit premium and the BVM Dilbit Value all to be 'converted from U.S. dollars per barrel to Canadian dollars per m3' using a conversion factor of 6.29234 barrels per m3 and 'the simple average of the daily actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rates for the month published by the Bank of Canada, rounded to 5 decimal places'.
tt: Bank of Canada Daily Exchange Rates

q: The International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) was adopted by the United Nations in 1948 and is used as the international standard for guiding work on national industrial classifications.
b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY BY THIS SESSION (abs.gov.au fetched as ordinary server-rendered HTML; the Preface sits on the volume's landing page and the following passages on its Introduction page). Preface: "International comparability has been enhanced by aligning the classification, as far as possible, with the upcoming revision of the International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) (Revision 4)." Introduction, under 'International standards': "The International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) was adopted by the United Nations in 1948 and is used as the international standard for guiding work on national industrial classifications." And: "Australia and New Zealand have for many years endeavoured to align their industrial classifications with the ISIC as far as possible. However, the degree of alignment able to be achieved is sometimes adversely affected by competing classification principles e.g. a different organisation or structure of Australian or New Zealand industry, or a lack of significance of some internationally recognised economic activities in the two economies." The parentage is stated for the predecessors too: the 1969 ASIC "was based at the broader levels on the ISIC", the 1970 NZSIC was "based on ISIC, Rev.2", and the driver for a single joint classification was "the need to update each country's classifications to align with ISIC, Rev.3 issued in 1990." Typed `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`: ISIC supplies the structure the classification is built against, and the ANZSIC volume ships correspondences to it.
tt: International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY BY THIS SESSION (abs.gov.au Introduction page, fetched as ordinary server-rendered HTML). Under 'Alignment with international standards': "In the interests of international statistical comparability, ANZSIC 2006 aligns with the ISIC and the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) at the subdivision level as far as practicable." The next paragraph makes this a design input rather than a remark: "In the ANZSIC review, close consideration was given to the work undertaken in recent years on the ISIC and the NAICS. Australia and New Zealand have been involved in international meetings reviewing the bases of these classifications. To the extent considered appropriate to Australian and New Zealand conditions, ANZSIC 2006 therefore reflects the latest international work on industrial classifications." The 'Changes from ANZSIC 1993' section then names NAICS twice as the corroborating precedent for specific structural decisions — the new Information Media and Telecommunications Division ("The proposed ISIC, Rev.4 and NAICS 2002 also recognise this as a separate Division") and the break-up of Property and Business Services into three divisions ("The three separate divisions again align with the proposed ISIC, Rev.4 and NAICS 2002"). Weaker than the ISIC edge — NAICS is a peer consulted for comparability, not a parent — but the alignment is asserted at a named level of the hierarchy and used to justify named divisions, which is more than 'consistent with'.
tt: North American Industry Classification System (NAICS)
tp: Statistics Canada, U.S. Office of Management and Budget / Economic Classification Policy Committee, and INEGI (Mexico)

q: Businesses in scope of EAS are determined based on their ANZSIC industry and institutional sector classifications
b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY BY THIS SESSION (ABS Australian Industry methodology, 2024-25, fetched as ordinary server-rendered HTML). Under 'Classifications': "Estimates in this release are classified by: Industry, in accordance with the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC), 2006 edition." ANZSIC is not decorative here — it defines the survey's scope as well as its output: "Businesses in scope of EAS are determined based on their ANZSIC industry and institutional sector classifications", the out-of-scope list is stated in ANZSIC subdivisions ("Entities classified to ANZSIC Subdivisions 62 Finance and 63 Insurance and superannuation funds"; "75 Public administration, 76 Defence and 96 Private households employing staff..."), and the rule for splitting a unit's reported data is stated in ANZSIC terms with numeric thresholds: "3% or more, where the industries of the primary and secondary activities are in the same ANZSIC Division. 2% or more, where the industries of the primary and secondary activities are in different ANZSIC Divisions." The release's own headline table is titled by ANZSIC Division.
tt: Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC)
tp: Australian Bureau of Statistics and Statistics New Zealand (Tatauranga Aotearoa)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY BY THIS SESSION (Stats NZ DataInfo+ item fetched in full; the passages sit in the 'Significant events impacting this study series' chronology, which is server-rendered and not behind the collapsed sections). 2007: "Sample re-optimised in response to the classification change from Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC96 to ANZSIC06). Survey designed and published on an ANZSIC06 basis. 2005 and 2006 data backdated on an ANZSIC06 basis." The adoption is dated: 1998: "The Annual Enterprise Survey sample based on the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) classification, replacing the New Zealand Standard Industrial Clasification (NZSIC)." [sic — 'Clasification' is the source's own typo]. And 2006: "Sample boost to help with the revisions due to the introduction of the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC06)." The 2012 entry then uses ANZSIC as the working unit of the survey's own documentation — "industries other than agriculture, forestry, and fishing division (ANZSIC06 division A)". Note the survey publishes at NZSIOC level 4, a New Zealand output classification layered on top of ANZSIC and not yet a node here; see `_dropped`.
tt: Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC)
tp: Australian Bureau of Statistics and Statistics New Zealand (Tatauranga Aotearoa)

tp: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)

tp: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)

tp: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)

tp: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)

tp: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)

tp: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)

tp: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY. Art. 52 caput establishes the RREO's scope and deadline ("abrangerá todos os Poderes e o Ministério Público, será publicado até trinta dias após o encerramento de cada bimestre"), and Art. 53's five incisos define its exact required content — including a cross-reference to the LRF's own definition of net current revenue ("receita corrente líquida, na forma definida no inciso IV do art. 2º") and to Art. 4º and Art. 50 for the interest and social-security demonstratives. This is genuine methodology, not merely a publication mandate — the report's structure and defined terms come from the statute itself, distinguishing this edge from `br-ibge-estimativas-populacao -> br-lei-8443` in `br-fpm-population.json`, which that file's own basis explicitly typed as `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on` because Lei 8.443 "compels the publication and fixes its deadline, and supplies no method." LC 101/2000 Arts. 52–53 supply the method.
tt: Lei Complementar nº 101, de 4 de maio de 2000 (Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal — LRF)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY. Art. 48 caput names the RGF, alongside the RREO, as one of the LRF's own transparency instruments. Art. 54 caput fixes who issues it and on what cadence ("Ao final de cada quadrimestre será emitido pelos titulares dos Poderes e órgãos referidos no art. 20 Relatório de Gestão Fiscal"), and its parágrafo único and incisos I–IV fix who signs it. Art. 55 caput and inciso I define the report's actual content as a comparison against the LRF's own legal limits ("comparativo com os limites de que trata esta Lei Complementar") — the limits themselves, and the definitions used to test compliance against them, are set elsewhere in the same statute, making this methodology rather than a bare publication mandate.
tt: Lei Complementar nº 101, de 4 de maio de 2000 (Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal — LRF)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, and minted on a three-document chain because NO SINGLE DOCUMENT STATES IT — the same treatment this corpus gave the New Zealand rating chain, where four statutory hops carry one edge. Stated plainly so a reader can judge it. (1) The decision itself, read via Wayback `id_` replay of the TCU's own PDF after portal.tcu.gov.br served a bot challenge, art. 1º: "Ficam aprovados, para o exercício de 2026, na forma dos Anexos I a X desta Decisão Normativa, os coeficientes individuais de participação no Fundo de Participação dos Municípios (FPM), previsto no art. 159, inciso I, alíneas “b”, “d”, “e” e “f”, da Constituição Federal, incluindo a Reserva instituída pelo art. 2º do Decreto-Lei 1.881, de 27 de agosto de 1981." (2) Its annexes, twenty-eight times, head the population column "População (fonte: IBGE, ref. 01/07/2025)" — AGENCY ONLY, plus a reference date that is the Estimativas release's own. (3) Lei 8.443/1992 art. 102 obliges publication of the population list "para os fins previstos no inciso VI do art. 1º desta Lei", art. 1º VI being the TCU's coefficient-fixing function. (4) IBGE's Estimativas methodology note closes it from the producer's side: "A partir de 1992, o IBGE passa a publicar no Diário Oficial da União - DOU, as Estimativas da População dos Municípios e Estados, em cumprimento ao Art. 102 da Lei nº 8.443, de 16.07.1992, para os fins previstos no inciso VI do Art. 1º da Lei nº 8.443." The relationship is documented; it is simply distributed across a decision, a statute and a methodology note rather than asserted in any one of them.
tt: Estimativas da População
tp: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)

q: As Estimativas da População residente nos Municípios, com data de referência em 1º de julho de 2025, foram calculadas com base nas Projeções da População do Brasil e Unidades da Federação, Revisão 2024, e nos totais populacionais dos Municípios enumerados pelos Censos Demográficos 2010 e 2022.

The note continues, on how the two censuses are used: "As populações recenseadas nos Municípios nesses dois últimos Censos Demográficos foram ajustadas e serviram de base para o estabelecimento da tendência de crescimento da população para as Estimativas da População até a data de referência, em 1º de julho de 2025." b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (methodology note, and the statute independently from planalto.gov.br). The note: "A partir de 1992, o IBGE passa a publicar no Diário Oficial da União - DOU, as Estimativas da População dos Municípios e Estados, em cumprimento ao Art. 102 da Lei nº 8.443, de 16.07.1992... Em 2013, foi publicada a Lei Complementar nº 143, de 17.07.2013, que altera o Art. 102 da Lei nº 8.443, estabelecendo que entidade competente do Poder Executivo Federal fará publicar no DOU, até o dia 31 de agosto de cada ano, a relação das populações dos Municípios..." The statute's own current text confirms it: "Art. 102. Entidade competente do Poder Executivo federal fará publicar no Diário Oficial da União, para os fins previstos no inciso VI do art. 1º desta Lei, a relação das populações: I - até 31 de dezembro de cada ano, no caso dos Estados e do Distrito Federal; II - até 31 de agosto de cada ano, no caso dos Municípios." `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on`: the Act compels the publication and fixes its deadline, and supplies no method.
tt: Lei nº 8.443, de 16 de julho de 1992 (Lei Orgânica do Tribunal de Contas da União)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A (planalto.gov.br, plain curl with a browser User-Agent, HTTP 200, 753,510 bytes). This is the edge br-ipca-fpe.json's own _dropped block recorded as NOT FOUND ("INPC is widely reported elsewhere as the index used to readjust INSS social-security benefits ... but no primary-source law or decree naming INPC for either purpose was located this session"), now closed from the statute's own text. Lei 8.213/1991 art. 41-A, inserted by Lei 11.430/2006: "O valor dos benefícios em manutenção será reajustado, anualmente, na mesma data do reajuste do salário mínimo, pro rata, de acordo com suas respectivas datas de início ou do último reajustamento, com base no Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor - INPC, apurado pela Fundação Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística - IBGE." `calculated_from` rather than `cites`: this is a stated indexation formula whose output — the readjusted value of every RGPS benefit in maintenance — is mechanically derived from INPC's published variation, the same shape br-ipca-fpe.json's own basis gives for br-lc-62-1989 -> br-ipca. The statute names both the index and its producing agency, which is the strongest form this corpus recognises. No reference_period is given: art. 41-A fixes the readjustment date by reference to the minimum wage's date and states no accumulation window, unlike Lei 14.663/2023 § 1º which does.
tt: Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (INPC)
tp: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A (planalto.gov.br, plain curl with a browser User-Agent, HTTP 200, 36,354 bytes). Lei 14.663/2023 art. 3º § 1º: "Os reajustes para a preservação do poder aquisitivo do salário mínimo corresponderão à variação do Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (INPC), calculado e divulgado pela Fundação Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), acumulada nos 12 (doze) meses encerrados em novembro do exercício anterior ao do reajuste." A second, independent statutory INPC dependency alongside br-lei-8213 -> br-inpc, and the more precisely specified of the two: it names the index, names IBGE as producer, and fixes the exact accumulation window. `calculated_from` because the inflation term of the minimum wage is arithmetically the accumulated INPC variation, not a contextual reference. The statute even documents its own fallback when the input is late (§ 2º: "o Poder Executivo federal estimará os índices dos meses não disponíveis"), which presupposes a mechanical dependency rather than a discretionary one.
tt: Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (INPC)
tp: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)

q: OS MINISTROS DE ESTADO DA PREVIDÊNCIA SOCIAL E DA FAZENDA ... tendo em vista o disposto ... no art. 41-A da Lei nº 8.213, de 24 de julho de 1991...
b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A (in.gov.br DOU text, HTTP 200, 104,885 bytes). The Portaria's preamble names the article by number: "OS MINISTROS DE ESTADO DA PREVIDÊNCIA SOCIAL E DA FAZENDA ... tendo em vista o disposto ... no art. 41-A da Lei nº 8.213, de 24 de julho de 1991..." `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites` because art. 41-A supplies the actual method the Portaria executes — which index (INPC), whose index (IBGE), on what date ("na mesma data do reajuste do salário mínimo"), and on what pro rata basis ("de acordo com suas respectivas datas de início ou do último reajustamento") — the same distinction br-fiscal-responsibility-law.json draws for br-rreo -> br-lc-101-2000 (statute supplies method) against br-fpm-population.json's br-ibge-estimativas-populacao -> br-lei-8443 (statute supplies only a mandate and a deadline). THIS EDGE IS ALSO THE ONLY ROUTE FROM THIS PORTARIA TO INPC, AND THAT IS THE POINT: the Portaria's full DOU text contains zero occurrences of "INPC" and names no index — it states only the outcome ("serão reajustados, a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2026, em 3,90%"). The index naming lives one hop upstream, here. A direct br-portaria-reajuste-inss -> br-inpc edge would assert something the document does not say and is deliberately not minted.
tt: Lei nº 8.213, de 24 de julho de 1991 (Planos de Benefícios da Previdência Social) — art. 41-A

q: ...tendo em vista o disposto ... no art. 41-A da Lei nº 8.213, de 24 de julho de 1991; na Lei nº 14.663, de 28 de agosto de 2023; no Decreto nº 12.797, de 23 de dezembro de 2025...
b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A (in.gov.br DOU text). The Portaria's preamble names the minimum-wage valorisation statute alongside its own enabling provisions: "...tendo em vista o disposto ... no art. 41-A da Lei nº 8.213, de 24 de julho de 1991; na Lei nº 14.663, de 28 de agosto de 2023; no Decreto nº 12.797, de 23 de dezembro de 2025..." `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on`: Lei 14.663 defines the minimum wage's own valorisation formula, not the benefit-readjustment method — the benefit method comes from art. 41-A of Lei 8.213 (see the separate edge). What Lei 14.663 supplies to this Portaria is the legal basis for the floor value it applies, and the operative number itself arrives via the decree, not via the statute, which is why this edge is typed weaker than the other two.
tt: Lei nº 14.663, de 28 de agosto de 2023 (política de valorização permanente do salário mínimo)

q: ...tendo em vista o disposto ... no Decreto nº 12.797, de 23 de dezembro de 2025...
b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY FROM BOTH ENDS, TIER A. The Portaria's preamble names the decree: "...tendo em vista o disposto ... no Decreto nº 12.797, de 23 de dezembro de 2025..." And, more strongly than a preamble citation, the decree's operative figure appears verbatim inside the Portaria's own text: Decreto 12.797/2025 art. 1º sets "o valor do salário mínimo será de R$ 1.621,00 (mil seiscentos e vinte e um reais)", and Portaria art. 2º applies that same number as the benefit floor — "não poderão ser inferiores a R$ 1.621,00 (mil seiscentos e vinte e um reais)". `uses_data_from`: the decree's published figure is a literal input carried into the Portaria's own provisions, confirmed by two independently fetched documents agreeing on the value rather than by either document's claim about itself.
tt: Decreto anual de fixação do salário mínimo (edição em vigor: Decreto nº 12.797, de 23 de dezembro de 2025)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A (planalto.gov.br, plain curl with a browser User-Agent, HTTP 200, 10,327 bytes). Decreto 12.797/2025's preamble: "O PRESIDENTE DA REPÚBLICA, no uso da atribuição que lhe confere o art. 84, caput, inciso IV, da Constituição, e tendo em vista o disposto na Lei nº 14.663, de 28 de agosto de 2023, e na Lei nº 15.077, de 27 de dezembro de 2024, DECRETA:" `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`, and the contrast with br-ipca-fpe.json's br-resolucao-cmn-5141 -> br-decreto-12079-2024 is exactly the reason: that edge was typed `cites` because the decree "delegates the choice and fixes no method of its own". Lei 14.663 is the opposite case — art. 3º states the whole computation the decree's single number is the output of ("o valor decorrerá da soma do índice de medida da inflação do ano anterior ... com o índice correspondente ao crescimento real do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) de 2 (dois) anos anteriores"), including the index, the accumulation window and the fallback rules. The decree publishes the result; the statute supplies the method.
tt: Lei nº 14.663, de 28 de agosto de 2023 (política de valorização permanente do salário mínimo)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A (STN's own FINBRA/SICONFI Cartilha PDF from siconfi.tesouro.gov.br, plain curl, HTTP 200, 952,735 bytes, genuine text PDF extracted with pdftotext -layout). b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A. The measures name the Budget Law in their own constitutive first article: 「为加快建立现代财政制度，建立权责清晰、财力协调、区域均衡的中央和地方财政关系，推进基本公共服务均等化，根据《中华人民共和国预算法》及其实施条例，制定《中央对地方均衡性转移支付办法》。」 ("…in accordance with the Budget Law of the People's Republic of China and its Implementing Regulations, these Measures … are formulated.") Corroborated a second time in 第十三条: 「依照《中华人民共和国预算法》及其实施条例、《财政违法行为处罚处分条例》等国家有关规定追究相应责任。」 TENSE: 「根据 … 制定」 is present and constitutive, not a past-tense acknowledgement -- unambiguous. `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on`: the Budget Law establishes the transfer-payment system and its equalisation objective (第十六条) but supplies no calculation method; every formula in this chain is the measures' own. That is the same distinction `br-ipca-fpe.json` draws when typing `br-fpe-dn-tcu -> br-lei-8443` as `cites` while typing the formula statute as `methodology_depends_on`.
tt: 中华人民共和国预算法 (Budget Law of the People's Republic of China)
tp: 全国人民代表大会常务委员会 (Standing Committee of the National People's Congress)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, and a correction to BRICS/G.1, which recorded that the Budget Report cites no document by name. It does cite the Budget Law, operatively -- this is the legal authority for spending before the NPC has approved the budget, not decorative compliance language: 「根据预算法规定，预算年度开始后，在全国人民代表大会批准本预算草案前，可安排下列支出：上一年度结转的支出；参照上一年同期的预算支出数额安排必须支付的本年度部门基本支出、项目支出，以及对下级政府的转移性支出；法律规定必须履行支付义务的支出，以及用于自然灾害等突发事件处理的支出。根据上述规定，结合中央部门和地方实际支出需要，中央财政安排了部分本级支出及对地方转移支付。」 ("In accordance with the provisions of the Budget Law, after the budget year begins and before the NPC approves this draft budget, the following expenditures may be arranged: … In accordance with the above provisions … the central finance authority has arranged part of its own-level expenditure and transfer payments to localities.") Corroborated in weaker compliance voice: 「认真落实预算法和人大预算审查监督有关要求」 and 「坚持预算法定，硬化预算约束，进一步全面深入实施好预算法」. A literal regex scan of the full extracted report text returned 4 hits for 预算法. b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, and the strongest single edge found for China this round. Ningxia's own first article names the central measures by exact bracketed title: 「为加快建立现代财政制度…推进基本公共服务均等化，根据《中华人民共和国预算法》及《中央对地方均衡性转移支付办法》，特制定自治区对市县均衡性转移支付办法。」 Restated in the covering notice: 「根据《中央对地方均衡性转移支付办法》等有关规定，经报请自治区人民政府研究同意，自治区财政厅修订了…」 `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`, because the provincial instrument does not merely reference the central one -- it REPLICATES its formula: Ningxia's own 「某县标准收支缺口财力补助=（市县标准收入-市县标准支出）×补助系数」 is structurally the central 第四条's standard-expenditure-minus-standard-revenue-times-coefficient form, re-expressed one tier down. That is genuine method inheritance, the same distinction `br-ipca-fpe.json` uses to type `br-fpe-dn-tcu -> br-lc-62-1989` as `methodology_depends_on`. TENSE: 「根据 … 特制定」 is present and constitutive.

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, and a documented instance of the supranational-to-national dependency REPORTS.md's own secondary objective is looking for -- a national statistical system stating, in its own text, that it was revised to conform to an international standard. Verbatim: 「2009年，联合国等五大国际组织颁布了国民经济核算新的国际标准——《国民账户体系2008》（以下简称2008年SNA）。目前，绝大部分发达国家和部分发展中国家已经开始执行2008年SNA。我国国民经济核算体系也需要做出相应的修订，使之与新的国际标准相衔接，提高国际可比性。」 ("In 2009, the United Nations and four other major international organisations promulgated the new international standard for national economic accounting — the System of National Accounts 2008 … China's national economic accounting system also needs to be revised accordingly, so as to align with the new international standard and improve international comparability.") The operative clause repeats the intent constitutively: 「实现与国民经济核算新的国际标准相衔接…我国对中国国民经济核算体系进行了全面系统的修订。」 TENSE NOTE, flagged because the sentence mixes them: the promulgation of the 2008 SNA is described in the past, but the alignment is stated in present-constitutive voice (「使之与新的国际标准相衔接」 — "so as to align it with the new international standard"), and the revision it justifies is the instrument being issued. The edge is sound on the alignment clause, not on the historical one. Unlike most China edges this round, the target is named by exact title AND edition year, so there is no version ambiguity of the kind that blocked the COICOP edge (see `_dropped`).

b: CORRA's published methodology defines a contingency fallback computed directly from the Bank's policy rate: "The fallback rate is equal to the Bank of Canada target for the overnight rate for that day plus the mean spread over the previous five business days between CORRA and the Bank of Canada target on those days." If technical issues prevent calculation by 11:00 ET, CORRA is set at this fallback rate. The methodology page works a numeric example beginning "Bank of Canada target for the overnight rate: 1.75 percent". Note the causality is unusual: the Bank targets the overnight rate that CORRA measures, so CORRA normally depends on the policy rate only economically - but the documented, mechanical dependency is this fallback.

The CanDeal Term CORRA Methodology states Term CORRA "is a forward-looking measurement of overnight CORRA for 1- and 3-month tenors, based on market-implied expectations from CORRA derivatives markets. The rate is calculated from 1- and 3-month CORRA futures trading on the Montreal Exchange", and that it "is designed to complement both overnight CORRA and the CORRA Compounded Index that are administered and published by the Bank of Canada." The contract specifications annexed to the methodology close the loop mechanically: the futures' "final settlement price... is 100 minus the compounded daily CORRA rate over the reference quarter" (and over the reference month for the one-month contract).
tt: Canadian Overnight Repo Rate Average (CORRA)

b: Section IV "Other guidance" of Guideline B-20 states: "This Guideline is complementary to, and should be read in conjunction with, other OSFI guidance" and then lists, among others, the "Capital Adequacy Requirements Guideline" and the "Leverage Requirements Guideline". B-20 also provides that where a lender fails to control residential mortgage risk, "OSFI can take, or require the FRFI to take, corrective measures... including... the discretionary authority to adjust the FRFI's capital requirements or authorized leverage ratio".
tt: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR) Guideline
tp: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions

b: Guideline B-20 defers to CMHC's published insurance rules for the debt-serviceability standard on insured mortgages: "for insured mortgages, the Canada Mortgage Housing Corporation (CMHC) defines GDS and TDS ratios and sets maximum GDS and TDS limits." It adds that "For insured residential mortgages, OSFI expects FRFIs to meet mortgage insurers' requirements in regard to debt serviceability" and that B-20 "complements... the Government of Canada's mortgage insurance guarantee framework, which establishes the rules for government-backed insured mortgages."
tt: CMHC Mortgage Loan Insurance – Homeowner and Small Rental Programs (eligibility requirements and premium schedule)

b: B-20 does not itself contain the stress-test number; it points at OSFI's separately announced calibration: "At a minimum, the qualifying rate for all uninsured mortgages should be the greater of the contractual mortgage rate plus a buffer, as set by the Superintendent or the minimum (or 'floor') rate, as set by the Superintendent", and "OSFI will review the calibration of the qualifying rate (both the buffer and floor) at least annually and will issue announcements if there are any calibration changes."
tt: Minimum Qualifying Rate for Uninsured Mortgages
tp: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions

b: Historical but explicitly documented. OSFI's February 18, 2020 news release states: "OSFI's mortgage underwriting guideline (B-20) sets the minimum qualifying rate for uninsured mortgages... currently the minimum qualifying rate is the higher of the contractual mortgage rate plus two percent, or the five-year benchmark rate published by the Bank of Canada." That five-year benchmark rate was the Bank of Canada 5-Year Benchmark Posted Mortgage Rate from the posted chartered bank rate table. The link was severed on June 1, 2021 when OSFI replaced the Bank of Canada benchmark with a fixed 5.25 percent floor.
tt: Interest Rates Posted for Selected Products by the Major Chartered Banks

tt: Mortgage Qualifying Rate (Benchmark Rate for Insured Mortgages)

b: Historical but explicitly documented in the same backgrounder, which describes the rule it was replacing: "borrowers taking on an insured mortgage must qualify at the greater of the: Borrower's Contract Rate... or Bank of Canada 5-Year Benchmark Posted Mortgage Rate, which is the mode of the posted 5-year conventional mortgage rates offered by the six largest banks." The document gives OSFI's and Finance's reason for dropping it: the posted rate "is also less representative of average contract rates as it only considers Canada's six largest banks, and the 'posted', and not 'actual' rates offered to borrowers by those banks."
tt: Interest Rates Posted for Selected Products by the Major Chartered Banks

q: The Minister of Finance sets the qualification rules for insured mortgages.
b: CMHC does not set its own qualification rules for insured mortgages; the Minister of Finance does. OSFI's May 2021 MQR letter states plainly: "The Minister of Finance sets the qualification rules for insured mortgages." The Department of Finance backgrounder describes the same framework: "Mortgage insurance standards include requirements for a minimum down payment, and maximum mortgage amortization period, along with other factors such as minimum credit scores and maximum debt servicing levels. The standards also include minimum qualifying rates for insured mortgages", and notes the review was conducted by Finance "in consultation with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, the Bank of Canada, and the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation."
tt: Minimum Qualifying Rate for Insured Mortgages (Government-Backed Mortgage Insurance Guarantee Framework)

b: The Bank of Canada does not observe these rates itself; the benchmark is built from mortgage insurers' application files. Department of Finance backgrounder: "The new Benchmark Rate will be: The weekly median 5-year fixed insured mortgage rate as calculated by the Bank of Canada from federally-backed mortgage insurance applications adjudicated by mortgage insurers; plus a buffer of 200 basis points to be set by the Minister of Finance." CMHC is the dominant federally backed insurer adjudicating those applications.
tt: CMHC Mortgage Loan Insurance – Homeowner and Small Rental Programs (eligibility requirements and premium schedule)

q: 1.1.4 Supervisory Target CET1 Capital Ratio (%) - Indicate the supervisory target CET1 capital ratio (including the capital conservation buffer, DSIB surcharge and domestic stability buffer as applicable) as set by the regulator for the member institution in accordance with the Capital Adequacy Requ
b: CDIC's premium scoring reads its capital inputs straight out of OSFI's capital framework. The 2026 Manual instructs: "1.1.4 Supervisory Target CET1 Capital Ratio (%) - Indicate the supervisory target CET1 capital ratio (including the capital conservation buffer, DSIB surcharge and domestic stability buffer as applicable) as set by the regulator for the member institution in accordance with the Capital Adequacy Requirements guideline (i.e., OSFI Target CET1 capital ratio (%) as set out in Schedule 10.010 - Ratio Calculations of the BCAR form)". Members must file with CDIC "the Basel Capital Adequacy Return (BCAR)" and "the Leverage Requirements Return (LRR form)" that they submitted "to the Superintendent... in accordance with the financial reporting instructions published by OSFI", and CDIC states that returns already filed with OSFI "by means of the RRS system" need not be refiled.

The same report also footnotes "Statistics Canada. The report's glossary defines the concept it uses throughout to segment the market by reference to the OSFI guideline: "Stress test: The stress test, introduced in January 2018 under OSFI's B-20 Guideline, requires borrowers with uninsured mortgages to qualify at the higher of the Bank of Canada's five-year benchmark rate or their mortgage rate plus 2%. A similar stress test was required for insured loans beginning in 2016." The glossary further defines chartered banks and federally regulated financial institutions by OSFI's supervisory perimeter, and the report's lender taxonomy separates "Non-bank OSFI regulated" lenders.

q: P is the gross dollar value, before deductions, of the payrolls of all employers in the province for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of its Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours, other than the payrolls of (i) employers not included in that survey, and (ii) employers in the following industry classifications, as defined by the North American Industry Classification System: (A) the elementary and secondary schools industry group, (B) the hospitals subsector, (C) the nursing and residential care facilities subsector, (D) the provincial and territorial public administration subsector, and (E) the local, municipal and regional public administration subsector
b: SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(y), the payroll-tax revenue base, makes SEPH a named term in a statutory formula: 'P is the gross dollar value, before deductions, of the payrolls of all employers in the province for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of its Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours, other than the payrolls of (i) employers not included in that survey, and (ii) employers in the following industry classifications, as defined by the North American Industry Classification System: (A) the elementary and secondary schools industry group, (B) the hospitals subsector, (C) the nursing and residential care facilities subsector, (D) the provincial and territorial public administration subsector, and (E) the local, municipal and regional public administration subsector'. `calculated_from` because P is a term in the formula, not a consideration — the same test that makes boc-bank-rate calculated_from the policy rate. Note the provision also carves out its own exclusions by NAICS classification, so the edge to `naics` is stated in the same sentence. SCOPE, stated because the section number alone overstates it: s. 8 sits in DIVISION 2 — Nova Scotia, and defines revenue base 'For the purpose of sections 3.71 to 3.9 of the Act', which are the Nova Scotia additional-equalization provisions. SEPH does NOT appear in the DIVISION 1 all-provinces revenue base at s. 5 — the phrase 'payrolls' occurs nowhere in ss. 1 through 8(1)(j), because the 2007 reform folded payroll taxes into the personal-income base. So this is the Equalization Program depending on SEPH through one division of the Regulations, not through the general formula.

q: Both the censuses and the sample surveys are aimed at producing a variety of information on specific CAP targets, as well as providing a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data.
b:
VERIFIED DIRECTLY BY THIS SESSION (2026-08-09) -- Eurostat's 'Farm structure (ef)' metadata page re-fetched first-hand, and the sentence now pinned to its section: it sits in section 3.4, Statistical concepts and definitions. "Both the censuses and the sample surveys are aimed at producing a variety of information on specific CAP targets, as well as providing a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data." Direction is FSDN -> FSS, as the original lead reasoned: a ~75 000-farm sample capped by Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 Article 5(3) at "105 000 for the Community" needs a population framework to extrapolate to the 3.5 million farms it claims to represent, and this record says the FSS supplies it. Typed `methodology_depends_on` rather than `uses_data_from`: what passes is a weighting/extrapolation framework, not FSS observations feeding into FSDN records. TWO CAVEATS, both stated rather than smoothed over. First, the evidence is ONE-SIDED: it is Eurostat asserting what its survey is used for, and DG AGRI's own FSDN page -- read in full this session -- names neither the Farm Structure Survey, nor integrated farm statistics, nor Regulation (EU) 2018/1091, nor Eurostat anywhere. The producer of the dependent product has not been found stating the dependency. Second, the quoted sentence still says FADN, the network's pre-2023 name; the node is minted under its current name, FSDN, so the edge crosses a rename. Nothing found this session suggests the extrapolation arrangement itself changed with the rename, but nothing found confirms it either -- a successor should look for the same statement in FSDN-era methodology (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2746 is the obvious place, since DG AGRI's page says it carries the farm-selection methodology).

CORROBORATED FROM THE RECEIVING SIDE, 2026-08-09 (closing G.64.md cheap check 3 / this file's own _open_questions item 4). The first caveat above -- that only Eurostat, the supplying side, had been found stating this dependency -- no longer holds. FSDN's own implementing regulation, Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2746 of 25 October 2024 ('laying down rules for the application of Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 setting up the Farm Sustainability Data Network...'), fetched directly from EUR-Lex (CELEX:32024R2746), states in Annex III ('Models and methods for selection plan preparation'): 'all relevant types and sizes of farming represented in the integrated farm statistics (IFS) census or survey are to be covered at the level of detail which provides representative results on important farm groups, within the limits of the sample size.' 'Integrated farm statistics' is the Farm Structure Survey's own legal name -- Regulation (EU) 2018/1091, which this node's own description cites as its re-founding instrument, is titled 'on integrated farm statistics'. Recital (5) of 2024/2746 cross-references the same instrument directly: 'These standard outputs need to be established by product and should align with the list of core structural data variables set out in Annex III to Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 of the European Parliament and of the Council.' So the FSDN sample-selection methodology names the FSS/IFS census as the population it must represent, on its own side of the relationship, independent of Eurostat's own metadata page. The second caveat (the edge crosses FADN's rename to FSDN) is unaffected -- 2024/2746 is itself an FSDN-era instrument and does not use the name FADN, so it does not help there either way.

b: RESOLVED AND VERIFIED DIRECTLY BY THIS SESSION (2026-08-09). The identification is documented after all -- by definitional property rather than by acronym, which is why three prior searches for the string 'IPCN' missed it. Eurostat's own methodological annex to the Joint Index, 'Remuneration and Pensions Calculation of the Joint Index in accordance with Annex XI of the EU Staff Regulations' (ec.europa.eu/eurostat/cache/metadata/Annexes/prc_colc_tot_esms_an_2.pdf, fetched in full this session), names the Luxembourg component as "the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) in the case of Luxembourg", sourced from "the Luxembourg national statistical office (Statec)", and then defines it: "The current Luxembourg national index of consumer prices came into effect in 1997. It complies with the HICP except that its weighting structure excludes the consumer spending of non-residents on Luxembourg territory." STATEC's own methodology document 'L'indice des prix a la consommation (IPC)' (statistiques.public.lu, /fr/methodologie/methodes/economie-finances/Prix/ipc/IPC-description.pdf, fetched in full this session) gives that exclusion as the SOLE difference between its two indices, and assigns it to the IPCN: "l'IPCN exclut les depenses de consommation finale effectuees par des non-residents sur le territoire economique luxembourgeois alors que l'IPCH les inclut", and "L'IPCN et l'IPCH sont etablis selon les memes principes methodologiques. Les deux indices se distinguent sur le seul point de leur couverture geographique." Since the two indices differ on exactly one property, and Eurostat states that property, the identification is unique: the Joint Index's Luxembourg CPI is the IPCN, not the IPCH. STATED LIMIT, per sec.3: no document read writes 'IPCN' and 'the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) in the case of Luxembourg' in the same sentence. This is an identification by matching definitions across two primary sources, not a citation. Recorded as such rather than as a quoted equivalence. MINOR DATE TENSION, logged not resolved: Eurostat dates the current national index to 1997, while STATEC writes that "le Luxembourg a decide, en janvier 2000, de reintroduire l'indice national pour les besoins de l'<<echelle mobile des salaires>>" -- consistent if the index existed from 1997 and was adopted for wage indexation in 2000, but neither document says so.
tt: Indice des prix à la consommation national (IPCN)
tp: Service central de la statistique et des études économiques (STATEC)

q: The Average Weekly Earnings for a month is the average weekly earnings of the Industrial Aggregate in Canada for the month as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act.
b: Employment Insurance Act s. 4(3) sets the MIE as the previous year's MIE 'multiplied by the ratio that the average for the 12-month period ending on April 30 in that preceding year of the Average Weekly Earnings for each month in that 12-month period bears to the average for the 12-month period ending 12 months prior to April 30 of that preceding year'. Section 4(5) defines the term: 'The Average Weekly Earnings for a month is the average weekly earnings of the Industrial Aggregate in Canada for the month as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act.' That series is the industrial aggregate average weekly earnings published by the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours.

q: Each year, certain personal income tax and benefit amounts are indexed to inflation using the Consumer Price Index data as reported by Statistics Canada.
b: The CRA page opens: 'Each year, certain personal income tax and benefit amounts are indexed to inflation using the Consumer Price Index data as reported by Statistics Canada.' The statutory mechanism is Income Tax Act s. 117.1(1)(b)(ii), which sets the adjustment factor as (A/B) - 1 where 'A is the Consumer Price Index for the 12 month period that ended on September 30 next before that year, and B is the Consumer Price Index for the 12 month period immediately preceding'; s. 117.1(4) defines that index as 'the Consumer Price Index for Canada, as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act' averaged over the twelve months of the period. The published indexation factors (2.0% for 2026, 2.7% for 2025, 4.7% for 2024, 6.3% for 2023) are the direct output and drive every indexed bracket threshold and credit amount in the CRA table. See also https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-117.1.html

q: The Wage Measure for a month is the average weekly wages and salaries of (a) the Industrial Aggregate in Canada for the month as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act.
b: Canada Pension Plan s. 18(1)(c) sets the Year's Maximum Pensionable Earnings for each year as the preceding year's YMPE multiplied by the ratio of the average Wage Measure for the twelve months ending 30 June of the preceding year to the same average a year earlier. Section 18(5) defines the term: 'The Wage Measure for a month is the average weekly wages and salaries of (a) the Industrial Aggregate in Canada for the month as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act.' That industrial-aggregate average weekly earnings series is the output of the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours. Section 18(6) further requires that the most recently published Statistics Canada revision of the Industrial Aggregate be used, and s. 18(7) requires the Minister to adjust the series, on the advice of the Chief Statistician, if Statistics Canada changes the time or content basis of the Industrial Aggregate by more than one per cent.

q: the regional rate of unemployment that applies to a claimant is ... the average of the seasonally adjusted monthly rates of unemployment for the last three-month period for which statistics were produced by Statistics Canada
b: Employment Insurance Regulations s. 17(1)(a): 'the regional rate of unemployment that applies to a claimant is ... the average of the seasonally adjusted monthly rates of unemployment for the last three-month period for which statistics were produced by Statistics Canada'; for the regions in sections 12 to 14 of Schedule I it is the greater of that three-month average and the corresponding 12-month average. Subsection 17(4) adds that the rates 'shall be obtained by using the regional rates of unemployment produced by Statistics Canada that incorporate an estimate of the rates of unemployment for status Indians living on Indian reserves.' Those seasonally adjusted regional unemployment rates are Labour Force Survey output.

q: Old Age Security payment amounts are reviewed each year in January, April, July and October to ensure they reflect cost of living increases, as measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI)
b: The Old Age Security payment amounts page states: 'Old Age Security payment amounts are reviewed each year in January, April, July and October to ensure they reflect cost of living increases, as measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI)' and that 'the quarterly adjustment for all OAS benefits, including the Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), is based on the difference between the average CPI for two periods of three months each'. The July-September 2026 worked example compares the average CPI for February to April 2026 (167.1) with the average for November 2025 to January 2026 (165.1), giving the 1.2% increase, and prints the monthly CPI values used. Rates increase but never decrease when the CPI falls.

q: A is the Consumer Price Index (within the meaning assigned by subsection 117.1(4)) for the 12-month period that ended on September 30 of the base taxation year, and B is the Consumer Price Index for the 12 month period preceding
b: Income Tax Act s. 122.61(5) requires that 'each amount expressed in dollars in subsection (1) shall be adjusted' by the factor (A/B) - 1 where 'A is the Consumer Price Index (within the meaning assigned by subsection 117.1(4)) for the 12-month period that ended on September 30 of the base taxation year, and B is the Consumer Price Index for the 12 month period preceding'. Subsection 117.1(4) in turn defines that index as the Consumer Price Index for Canada published by Statistics Canada under the Statistics Act. This indexes the base amounts, both phase-out thresholds and the child disability supplement.

q: un prélèvement d'office opéré sur le budget général de l'Etat dont le taux est fixé annuellement dans la loi de finances
b: The organic decentralization law's Article 250 institutes the 'fonds de péréquation des collectivités locales' and Article 252 states it is funded by 'un prélèvement d'office opéré sur le budget général de l'Etat dont le taux est fixé annuellement dans la loi de finances' — i.e. the organic law itself designates the annual Finance Law as the instrument that sets the fund's actual take rate/amount each year. The FY2025 Finance Law's Article 21 line item 712 ('Péréquation Collectivités', 402,261,680 FCFA) is exactly that designated annual act: it is not merely citing the fund for context, it is the yearly mechanism Article 252 names as the fund's funding source, applied. That is a genuine data/figure dependency (the budget line's existence and legal basis flow from Article 252's designation) rather than a loose contextual reference, so uses_data_from is chosen over cites. Not calculated_from, since the 402,261,680 FCFA figure is not itself derived by a stated formula from anything in the organic law — the organic law sets the mechanism (that a rate is fixed annually in the finance law), not the rate itself.

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, and this REINSTATES the edge BRICS/G.1 explicitly drafted and then discarded. G.1's rejection was correct on the evidence it had -- it could find no verbatim passage in FC16's own text citing Article 280 by number, and preferred an honest `deferred` note to a plausible-but-unsupported edge. The passage exists, and it is the opening substantive sentence of the Report. FC16 Volume I, para 1.2, verbatim: "In pursuance of clause (1) of Article 280 of the Constitution of India and the provisions of the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951 (Act No. 33 of 1951), the President of India constituted the FC-16 vide Notification S.O. 5533(E) dated 31 December 2023 (Annexure 1.1). The Commission was mandated to make its recommendations for the five-year period commencing on 1 April 2026 and ending on 31 March 2031." That is an in-text citation naming the article and clause, in the dependent document's own body, in Chapter 1 "Constitution and Composition of the Commission" -- not the inference G.1 refused. `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on`: Article 280 constitutes the Commission and defines its remit; it supplies no devolution method, which is the Commission's own to devise. Recorded at length because the sequence is instructive -- the standard held, and the edge was real; the reconciliation was reading the dependent document more carefully, not relaxing the rule.
tt: Article 280, Constitution of India — "Finance Commission"
tp: Government of India, Ministry of Law and Justice (Legislative Department)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, from an official Gazette instrument's own operative text -- the strongest possible form of this citation, since the Order IS the exercise of the constitutional power it names. Verbatim: "S.O. 5533(E).— The following order made by the President is to be published for general information: — ORDER — In pursuance of clause (1) of article 280 of the Constitution read with the provisions of the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951 (33 of 1951), the President is pleased to constitute a Finance Commission…". TENSE: present and constitutive. `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on` for the same reason as the edge above -- the article confers the power and defines the remit without supplying a method. Note that the Order also names the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951 in the same breath; that statute has no corpus node and is recorded in `_dropped` as a lead.
tt: Article 280, Constitution of India — "Finance Commission"
tp: Government of India, Ministry of Law and Justice (Legislative Department)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY. FC16 names the constituting Order by its Gazette number in Volume I para 1.2 -- "the President of India constituted the FC-16 vide Notification S.O. 5533(E) dated 31 December 2023 (Annexure 1.1)" -- and then reproduces the Order's terms of reference in full, introducing them at para 1.8 with "As per the order constituting the FC-16, its ToR is as follows: 'The Commission shall make recommendations as to the following matters, namely: …'", with the Order itself carried as Annexure 1.1. `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`: the Order does not merely authorise the Commission, it fixes the questions the Report must answer and the award period it must cover, and the Report's structure follows those terms directly -- the Order supplies the scope the Report's method is built to satisfy. That is the same distinction `br-ipca-fpe.json` draws between a statute that grants authority (`cites`) and one that determines what must be computed (`methodology_depends_on`).

Volume I para 8.85, on the Population criterion carrying a 17.5 per cent weight: "In keeping with the longstanding practice ... we continue to include population among the criteria. In conformity with the uniform recommendation by nearly all States, we implement this criterion by awarding each State an allocation based on its share in the Census 2011 total population of the twenty-eight States. We assign a weight of 17.5 per cent to this criterion. We note here that whenever any of our variables are combined with population, we rely on the 2011 Census figures. In this respect, we have fully transitioned from the 1971 Census population to the 2011 Census population data." The Technical Note states it inside the formula itself: "Denoting by Nk the population of State k (k = 1, 2, … 28) as per the 2011 Census, we have, (ii) C1j = …". The Demographic Performance criterion depends on it too, para 8.88: "we set the per capita devolution to a State in proportion to the inverse of its population growth between 1971 and 2011 Censuses. We convert this per capita devolution into total by multiplying it by the 2011 population." And a table source line reads "Source: Reports of FC-11 to FC-15; Census of India 2001 and 2011." `uses_data_from` rather than `calculated_from`: the census figures are a direct published input to two weighted criteria, but the devolution shares are the output of a multi-criterion formula rather than a mechanical derivation from population alone.

The column it annotates reproduces FC16 Volume I Table 8.9 digit for digit: "Andhra Pradesh 4.217 | Arunachal Pradesh 1.354 | Assam 3.258 | Bihar 9.948 | Chhattisgarh 3.304 | Goa 0.365 | Gujarat 3.755 | Haryana 1.361 | Himachal Pradesh 0.914 | … | Uttar Pradesh 17.619 | Uttarakhand 1.141 | West Bengal 7.215" against FC16's own "Andhra Pradesh 4.217 / Arunachal Pradesh 1.354 / Assam 3.258 / Bihar 9.948 / Chhattisgarh 3.304 / Goa 0.365 / Gujarat 3.755 / Haryana 1.361 / Himachal Pradesh 0.914 / Jharkhand 3.357 / Karnataka 4.131 / Kerala 2.382 / Madhya Pradesh 7.347 / Maharashtra 6.441 …". `uses_data_from` rather than `cites`: the shares are literal computational inputs to the state-wise distribution the annex publishes, not a background reference. Appendix 2. The data for 2023-24 is taken from Statement 18 of Union Budget". q: Under sub-section (1) of section 45ZA of the RBI Act, the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, determines the inflation target in terms of the Consumer Price Index (CPI), once in every five years. This target would be notified in the Official Gazette.
b: VERIFIED, BUT WITH A WEAKNESS STATED EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN SILENTLY UPGRADED -- read this basis before relying on the edge. BRICS/G.1 scoped `in-rbi-act-45za` deliberately narrowly, to only what Section 45ZA's own text establishes, because it could not verify the notified target behind an RBI bot-wall and a CAPTCHA-gated gazette search. This round did NOT retrieve the literal signed gazette instrument either (S.O. 2088(E) -- see `_dropped` for the full record of attempts). What it did retrieve is the same statement from TWO INDEPENDENT PRIMARY GOVERNMENT-OF-INDIA PUBLISHERS. Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Finance, 5 August 2016: "Under sub-section (1) of section 45ZA of the RBI Act, the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, determines the inflation target in terms of the Consumer Price Index (CPI), once in every five years. This target would be notified in the Official Gazette." and "Determination and notification of Inflation Target — In exercise of the powers conferred by section 45ZA of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the Central Government, in consultation with RBI, has fixed the inflation target … Inflation Target: Four per cent. Upper tolerance level: Six per cent. Lower tolerance level: Two per cent." And the Reserve Bank's own Monetary Policy Overview: "Under Section 45ZA, the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, determines the inflation target in terms of the Consumer Price Index (CPI), once in five years and notifies it in the Official Gazette." THE MECHANISM IS ALSO CURRENT, which matters for tense: "In its second review, on March 25, 2026, the Central Government retained the inflation target and the tolerance band for the next 5-year period – April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2031." TWO EXPLICIT LIMITS ON THIS EDGE: (1) the citation comes from the Government's own explanatory statements ABOUT section 45ZA, not from the section's four corners nor from a retrieved gazette instrument; (2) the "(Combined)" qualifier is NOT evidenced anywhere reachable and is deliberately absent from this basis and from the node -- every primary text retrieved says "Consumer Price Index (CPI)" without it. `cites` rather than `uses_data_from` precisely because of limit (1): a stronger type would assert a computational relationship the retrieved documents do not themselves state.
tt: Consumer Price Index (CPI), Base: 2024=100
tp: Government of India, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), National Statistics Office (NSO)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY from the node's OWN release document, and available since BRICS/G.1 without being drawn -- the single cheapest edge in this round. The July 2026 CPI press release, which is `in-mospi-cpi`'s own url, states verbatim: "The CPI (Base: 2024=100) series is aligned with the United Nations' Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018, comprising 12 Divisions, 43 Groups, 92 Classes and 162 Subclasses." That sentence names the classification, its issuing body, AND the edition -- satisfying the edition rule outright, with no companion document required and no inference. It has been quoted in the `in-mospi-cpi` node description since G.1; what was missing was the edge, not the evidence. `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`: COICOP 2018 supplies the index's own classification structure down to the sub-class level, which is method, not reference. Corroborated independently by MoSPI's expert-group report (see the next edge). WEAKNESS STATED: the release says "aligned with", and the expert-group report elaborates that the series is "mostly aligned" -- India uses 12 Divisions against COICOP 2018's 15, with documented mapping compromises where household-survey items could not be mapped unambiguously. The dependency is real and named; the conformance is partial, and this corpus has no relationship type expressing partial conformance, so the qualification is recorded here.
tt: Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP 2018)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, edition named repeatedly. §3.3: "To enhance credibility and to ensure global comparability of Indian CPI, the latest structure of Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018 will be adopted in the CPI 2024 series." §2.3: "CPI 2024 – The latest classification framework is COICOP 2018. The CPI 2024 series is mostly aligned with COICOP 2018 with 12 Divisions, 43 Groups, 92 Classes and 162 Sub-classes." §4.1.5: "EG recommended for mapping HCES items as per COICOP 2018 in CPI 2024." This is the methodology document that DECIDES the classification the CPI release then reports using, so the two edges into `un-coicop-2018` are complementary rather than duplicative -- one records what the published index is built on, the other records the instrument that chose it. `methodology_depends_on` on the same reasoning as the release-level edge.
tt: Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP 2018)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, with the edition named and the manual applied NORMATIVELY rather than cited for colour -- it supplies the menu of options from which MoSPI picks its treatment. §4.6.5: "The procedure is fully consistent with the principles of the IMF CPI Manual (2020) and supports a smooth, stable, and operationally feasible implementation of the chain-base CPI." §5.3.2 and §5.3.4 go further and take a decision from it: "This is one of the three methods prescribed in the Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods 2020 (page 35) in case, if the price of social security transfers decreases from some positive amount to zero." followed by the three methods and MoSPI's choice, "Method 1: To use a zero price and adjust the weight during next update. (Proposed for new series of CPI)". §5.4.2 quotes the manual's paragraph 2.60 verbatim. The full title and year are given, with page and paragraph references (p.35, paras 2.60, 2.72). NODE IDENTITY CHECKED before minting: the `cpi-manual` node's own description identifies it as the 2020 edition updating the 2004 ILO-managed predecessor, matching what the Indian document names -- had the node been the 2004 edition, the edition rule would have required refusing this edge. Note the pleasing symmetry with the Russian side of this round: `ru-rosstat-cpi-methodology-915 -> cpi-manual` rests on the same manual, named with the same year, in a document of the same kind.
tt: Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods
tp: IMF, ILO, OECD, Eurostat, UNECE and the World Bank

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, edition named, and it closes the question BRICS/G.2 had to leave open. Chapter 2's opening sentence: "As per recommendations of System of National Accounts (SNA)-2008, NAD industry-wise estimates of GDP are compiled using institutional sector approach. All resident institutional units are allocated to one and only one of the following five institutional sectors: i. The non-financial corporation sector; ii. The financial corporation sector; iii. The general government sector; ..." The edition is explicit, the compiler named is the National Accounts Division itself, and the claim is about how India's GDP estimates ARE compiled rather than how they might be. `methodology_depends_on`: "as per recommendations of" introduces the sectoral framework actually used. THE SCOPE LIMIT IS THE REASON THIS EDGE IS MINTED FROM A NEW NODE RATHER THAN FROM `in-mospi-nas`: the quote is from a companion methodology report of the National Accounts Division, not from the body of the National Accounts Statistics publication, whose own release text still says only "System of National Accounts (SNA)" with no year. Attaching the edge to `in-mospi-nas` would put a citation in that node's mouth that its document does not make -- so the report is minted as its own node instead, exactly as the Russian side handles `ru-rosstat-osm-233-household-accounts`. Secondary corroboration in the same PDF (§1.1, "consistent with the System of National Accounts (SNA) guidelines") is unversioned and would not support an edge alone.
tt: System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008)
tp: United Nations, European Commission, IMF, OECD and World Bank

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A. NIC-2025's Introduction: "The classification aligns with the International Standard Industrial Classification (ISIC Rev. 5) while addressing specific features of the Indian economy such as the informal sector, agriculture, renewable energy, and the growing digital economy." And under Salient Features: "Based on ISIC Rev. 5: NIC-2025 is aligned with the latest international standard, ISIC Revision 5, ensuring structural and conceptual comparability up to the 4-digit class level." `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`: the national classification's structure IS the international one to four digits, which is as strong as a classification dependency gets. NODE-IDENTITY CHECK, and the reason no edition problem arises: the corpus's `isic` node is deliberately the unversioned FAMILY node -- its own description calls it "the acknowledged parent of most national industrial classifications, including ANZSIC and its two predecessors" -- so it is designed to receive citations of any revision, unlike `sna-2008`/`sna-2025` and `un-coicop-2018`/`un-coicop-hbs-1999`, which are edition-split. Recorded because a future round may reasonably propose splitting `isic` by revision, at which point this edge would need re-pointing to a Rev. 5 node, and NIC 2008's separately documented dependency on ISIC Rev. 4 would become mintable as well.
tt: International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, first-person and edition-named. "The compilation of BoP data is based on the IMF guidelines set out in its Balance of Payments Manual (BPM) ... IMF has recently brought out the Sixth Edition of BPM, i.e., BPM6 which has suggested revised compilation procedure as well as new format of standard presentation of BoP statistics. ... Accordingly, from this quarter (Q4 of 2010-11), BoP data are presented in the revised format as per BPM6." The RBI's own statistical tables carry it in their headings -- "Statement I: Standard Presentation of BoP as per BPM6 (US$ million)" -- and a table note reads "Changes in Reserve Assets are included under the Financial Account as recommended by the BPM 6." `methodology_depends_on`: BPM6 supplies both the compilation procedure and the presentation format of India's published BoP. TENSE WEAKNESS STATED HONESTLY, since this project's own spec insists on it: the verified article is the Q4 2010-11 transition issue, so its central sentence documents the moment of adoption. That is a PAST-tense event, and on its own would be exactly the kind of past arrangement this corpus refuses to treat as a live dependency. It is minted because two independent present-tense confirmations exist: the RBI's statistical statements are still headed "as per BPM6", and the Ministry of Finance's September 2025 external-debt report treats BPM6 as the current framework. A current RBI quarterly BoP press release would remove the caveat entirely and is a clean lead -- blocked only by the `rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/` bot-wall.
tt: Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, Sixth Edition (BPM6)

q: 1 World Economic Outlook, October 2020
b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, and structurally the most important edge in this file: `in-fc15-report` sits inside India's main eleven-node component, so this single citation is what attaches the whole Finance Commission cluster -- Constitution, Commission reports, Explanatory Memoranda, Union Budget, RBI State Finances, CAG -- to the international layer. FC15 Volume I cites the WEO in two footnotes supporting its macroeconomic narrative: "1 World Economic Outlook, October 2020" and "4 World Economic Outlook October 2020, International Monetary Fund". `uses_data_from` rather than `methodology_depends_on`, deliberately: the WEO supplies comparator data and growth figures the Commission reasons from; it is not a standard the Commission's methodology conforms to. ON THE EDITION QUESTION, which the research flagged and which is worth settling here as a corpus rule: `imf-weo` is NOT edition-split and should not be, because the WEO is a RECURRING PUBLICATION, not a standard with successor editions held as separate nodes. This corpus models a recurring release as one node covering all its issues -- `br-ipca` covers every month, `cn-nbs-statistical-communique` every year -- so citing the October 2020 issue is like citing a particular month of a monthly index, and points at the series node correctly. That is a different situation from SNA 2008 versus SNA 2025, which are successive STANDARDS deliberately held apart. WEAKNESS STATED: this is a footnote citation, the weakest form of dependency in this project's taxonomy. A third mention (the source line of Figure 2.2, "Sources: IMF, World Economic Outlook, and staff calculations") is unversioned and would not qualify alone.
tt: World Economic Outlook (WEO)

q: International Labour Office. 2004. Consumer Price Index Manual: Theory and Practice. Geneva.
b: The Canadian Consumer Price Index Reference Paper (catalogue 62-553-X) Chapter 4 states the three criteria the CPI product and geographical classifications are designed to meet, and footnotes them directly to 'ILO et al. (2004), paragraph 3.144' — i.e. the Consumer Price Index Manual: Theory and Practice, predecessor of the current CPI Manual: Concepts and Methods. The Reference Paper's bibliography lists the manual in full: 'International Labour Office. 2004. Consumer Price Index Manual: Theory and Practice. Geneva.' This is StatCan sourcing a design rule of the Canadian CPI to the international manual, not merely listing it.
tt: Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods
tp: IMF, ILO, OECD, Eurostat, UNECE and the World Bank

q: QCEW currently uses the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) to classify industries for establishments.
b: The QCEW Overview, under 'Industry Classification', states: 'QCEW currently uses the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) to classify industries for establishments.' QCEW publishes down to the 6-digit NAICS industry level and aggregates up through NAICS industry groups, sectors and supersectors, so the classification is the publication structure of the release, not an incidental reference.
tt: North American Industry Classification System (NAICS)
tp: Statistics Canada, U.S. Office of Management and Budget / Economic Classification Policy Committee, and INEGI (Mexico)

q: The production estimates are published for 198 separate industries and 89 aggregates to provide a variety of levels of detail useful for analysis of industrial economic performance, using the North American Industrial Classification System.
b: The Statistics Canada survey record for Gross Domestic Product by Industry - National (Monthly), record no. 1301, states: 'The production estimates are published for 198 separate industries and 89 aggregates to provide a variety of levels of detail useful for analysis of industrial economic performance, using the North American Industrial Classification System.' The same record lists 'North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Canada 2017 Version 3.0' among its formal documentation.
tt: North American Industry Classification System (NAICS)
tp: Statistics Canada, U.S. Office of Management and Budget / Economic Classification Policy Committee, and INEGI (Mexico)

b: The Methodological Guide: Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts (catalogue 13-607-X) states: 'The CSMA is built using three main international macroeconomic accounting frameworks... The "Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, Sixth Edition" is the underlying framework used to compile Canada's Balance of Payments and International Investment Position.' The guide adds that using these internationally adopted manuals 'ensures the resulting statistics are consistent and comparable with macroeconomic accounts compiled in the United States, Australia, the European Union and other countries.'
tt: Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, Sixth Edition (BPM6)

q: Government Finance Statistics Manual
b: The same passage of the Methodological Guide: Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts names the third of the three frameworks: 'The "Government Finance Statistics Manual" is the underlying framework used to compile Canada's Government Finance Statistics.' Canadian Government Finance Statistics is one of the seven account categories that make up the CSMA.
tt: Government Finance Statistics Manual (GFSM 2014)

q: Option 2 - Adapt IPSAS principles when developing future standards
b: On 5 May 2020 PSAB approved 'Option 2 - Adapt IPSAS principles when developing future standards' as its International Strategy: PSAB continues to issue Canadian Public Sector Accounting Standards, but future standards are based on the principles in the corresponding IPSAS, and PSAB will only amend an IPSAS principle where it is contrary to PSAB's own Conceptual Framework. PSAB has separately proposed modifying the Canadian public sector GAAP hierarchy in Section PS 1150 to position IPSAS as the go-to framework where PSAB has not issued a specific standard.
tt: International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS)
tp: International Public Sector Accounting Standards Board (IPSASB), IFAC

q: The need for internationally comparable information means that the census aims to comply with international standards set at global and regional levels. The United Nations reviews and sets census recommendations and principles every 10 years to ensure international consistency.

The United Nations reviews and sets census recommendations and principles every 10 years to ensure international consistency.' It adds that under the revised Statistics Act 'the census will follow the highest international standards'. Caveat: StatCan describes the UN standard by its function and revision cycle rather than naming Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses by title.
tt: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses
tp: United Nations Statistics Division (Department of Economic and Social Affairs)

The dependency is load-bearing enough that NAICS revisions force revisions of the statistics themselves — the guide notes that adopting NAICS 2022 required a historical revision of SEPH estimates back to 2001, and that businesses which cannot be assigned a NAICS code are excluded from all variables except employment.
tt: North American Industry Classification System (NAICS)
tp: Statistics Canada, U.S. Office of Management and Budget / Economic Classification Policy Committee, and INEGI (Mexico)

Nqazidja [Ngazidja] / 27,4%... Ndzouani / 25,7%... Mwali / 9,4%'. Those four figures match this organic law's Article 8 formula exactly (Union 37,50% / Ngazidja 27,4% / Anjouan 25,7% / Mohéli 9,4%), and Article 7 of the organic law states the mechanism 'ne peut être modifié que par une loi organique' (can only be amended by [another] organic law) -- i.e. the annual finance law's residual-split percentages are calculated per this organic law's formula, not independently set each year.
