q: établit chaque mois un indice des prix à la consommation conformément aux dispositions du Règlement (CE) n° 2494/95 du Conseil du 23 octobre 1995 relatif aux indices des prix à la consommation harmonisés
b: Règlement grand-ducal du 20 décembre 1999, Art. 1er: STATEC 'établit chaque mois un indice des prix à la consommation conformément aux dispositions du Règlement (CE) n° 2494/95 du Conseil du 23 octobre 1995 relatif aux indices des prix à la consommation harmonisés' [establishes monthly a consumer price index in accordance with the provisions of Council Regulation (EC) No 2494/95 of 23 October 1995 on harmonised indices of consumer prices]. Same shape as de-destatis-national-accounts -> esa-2010: a binding EU regulation supplies the definitions and methodology a national release conforms to, not figures. eurostat-hicp's own description states it is 'calculated according to a harmonised approach and definitions as laid down in Regulations and Recommendations' -- the same regulatory framework named here. Not extended to lu-statec-ipcn: Art. 1er says the IPCN merely 'se conforme aux mêmes principes et concepts méthodologiques' [conforms to the same methodological principles and concepts] as the IPCH, without itself being subject to Regulation 2494/95 -- a Research.1 §5a 'comparable with' shape, not a documented dependency, so no edge is drawn for the IPCN side.
tt: Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP)

tt: Report about Inflation and Consumer Price Indices

tt: Loi organique n° 111-14 relative aux régions

q: Administrative information for total gross monthly payrolls and the total number of employees for the last pay period in the month are obtained from payroll deduction (PD7 form) accounts maintained by Canada Revenue Agency.
b: Record 2612, Data sources: 'The statistics compiled by SEPH are based on a census of administrative records for all in-scope establishments with employees that can be found on the Business Register. Administrative information for total gross monthly payrolls and the total number of employees for the last pay period in the month are obtained from payroll deduction (PD7 form) accounts maintained by Canada Revenue Agency.' A census of these records rather than a sample of employers, which makes this the strongest available characterisation short of calculated_from. Held at uses_data_from because SEPH applies estimation on top — the same record describes model groups and a Business Payrolls Survey filling gaps — so the payroll figure is not arithmetic on the remittances alone.
tt: CRA payroll deduction (PD7) accounts

q: In this methodology, a model that describes the relationship between estimated sales coming from the MSM and sales coming from the Goods and Services Tax (GST) data at a small level of geography is combined with traditional estimates obtained from the weighted MSM sample.
b: Record 2101, Use of Administrative Data: 'In an attempt to alleviate response burden, especially for small businesses, the MSM derives sales data for low-revenue establishments from Goods and Service Tax (GST) files using a ratio estimator.' The word 'derives' plus a named estimator is a direct-input claim; it applies to a stated subset of establishments rather than the whole, which is why this is uses_data_from and not calculated_from.
tt: Goods and Services Tax (GST) administrative files

q: As part of the Integrated Business Statistics Program (IBSP), T1 tax data are used for unincorporated businesses, T2 tax data for incorporated businesses, T3010 tax data for registered charities and T5013 tax data for partnerships. b: Record 2103, Data sources: 'As part of the Integrated Business Statistics Program (IBSP), T1 tax data are used for unincorporated businesses, T2 tax data for incorporated businesses, T3010 tax data for registered charities and T5013 tax data for partnerships. Data replacement may be used to correct outliers or to replace partially or completely missing data. Tax data may also be used to reconcile survey data.' b: THE WEAKEST EDGE IN THIS SLICE, and flagged rather than buried. The NOC 2021 introduction states: 'It is important to note that the redesign of the NOC can have significant implications for several Surveys, such as the Labour Force Survey (LFS), and ESDC programs such as the Temporary Foreign Worker Program and Employment Insurance program.' This is a statement that a revision reaches the LFS, not a statement that the LFS uses the NOC, and the direction has to be read out of it rather than off it. It is taken on the precedent already set for boc-prime-rate -> boc-policy-rate, which rests on the Bank of Canada's word 'affects' and was accepted as `uses_data_from` on exactly that reasoning. It is also corroborated structurally by NOC being 'the departmental standard for data collection and dissemination for occupations at Statistics Canada' as of 10 August 2021. The clean version of this edge is a passage in the LFS's own record 3701 saying it codes occupation to NOC; that passage has not been retrieved, and the `_dropped` block records it as the lead to close.

q: El Censo de Población y Vivienda del Instituto Nacional de Estadística, Geografía e Informática (INEGI) (2020) contabilizó una población de 779,566 habitantes en el municipio de Acapulco de Juárez, que representan el 22.0% de la población estatal
b: Acapulco's own Plan Municipal de Desarrollo Urbano opens its socio-demographic diagnosis by taking the municipality's population count directly from the 2020 census. Verbatim: "El Censo de Población y Vivienda del Instituto Nacional de Estadística, Geografía e Informática (INEGI) (2020) contabilizó una población de 779,566 habitantes en el municipio de Acapulco de Juárez, que representan el 22.0% de la población estatal". Independently corroborated by the Bienestar municipal profile for Acapulco de Juárez (https://www.gob.mx/cms/uploads/attachment/file/1061187/12001_AcapulcoDeJuarez_2026.pdf), whose footnotes carry the identical census citations. Additionally, pMDU section 4.5.3 (Población Económicamente Activa) — the section round 2 could see only in the table of contents — derives Acapulco's PEA, employed and unemployed counts from the 2020 census and INEGI's occupation tabulations. Verbatim: "Del Censo de Población y Vivienda (2020) y de los Tabulados de INEGI, se señala que para el municipio de Acapulco la PEA3 representa el 66% de la población total de más de 15 años; el 98% de la PEA corresponde a la población ocupada con 377,351 personas y el 2% a población desocupada corresponde a 7,626 acapulqueños". The section's Table 27 source line reads "Fuente: Elaboración propia CONURBA, 2021; con base en Tabulados de Ocupación, INEGI; Censo de Población y Vivienda INEGI, 2020".
tt: Censo de Población y Vivienda / Population and Housing Census

q: There shall be levied for the benefit of the funds of regional councils an amount equal to five per cent of the rates levied under section 73 on all rateable property situated in local authority areas. ... The amount referred to in subsection (1) shall be collected by a local authority council situated in the region of the regional council concerned ... and paid over to the regional council.
b: Local Authorities Act 23 of 1992, s.77(1)-(2): 'There shall be levied for the benefit of the funds of regional councils an amount equal to five per cent of the rates levied under section 73 on all rateable property situated in local authority areas. ... The amount referred to in subsection (1) shall be collected by a local authority council situated in the region of the regional council concerned ... and paid over to the regional council.' A regional council's funds under Regional Councils Act s.33(1)(a) ('moneys appropriated by law for purposes of the funds of the regional council') include this amount, which is mechanically computed as a fixed 5% of the local-authority property rates levied under the Local Authorities Act s.73 -- the clearest documented municipal-to-regional fiscal-transfer formula found in this round's research.
tt: Local Authorities Act 23 of 1992
tp: Government of the Republic of Namibia

Quote establishing the link: "Les municipalités bénéficiaires doivent utiliser les fonds reçus selon un mécanisme prévu par le Décret n°2007-184/PRN/MI/D du 25 mai 2007 qui dispose dans son article 6 que 90% des fonds sont destinés aux investissements, 5% au fonctionnement et 5% à l'appui technique aux municipalités..." The décret's applicability is contingent on Code Minier Art. 95 having generated the 15%-to-communes fund pool in the first place, so the décret's spending mechanism depends on the mining code's revenue-sharing formula rather than existing independently of it.

q: (4) The database must include, in relation to each rating unit within the local authority’s district,— (a) all information that relates to the unit that is included in the district valuation roll for the district
b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (Local Government (Rating) Act 2002, version as at 27 November 2025, read from the Parliamentary Counsel Office's own PDF replayed byte-for-byte through the Wayback `id_` endpoint because legislation.govt.nz's WAF returns HTTP 202 with zero bytes to non-browser clients; pypdf-extracted, 129 pages). The chain is entirely in statute, in four hops. s.13(3): "For the purposes of this section, the rateable value of the land— (a) must be— (i) the annual value of the land; or (ii) the capital value of the land; or (iii) the land value of the land; and (b) must be identified in the local authority's funding impact statement as the value for setting a general rate." s.5 pins each of those three to the other Act: "capital value has the meaning set out in section 2(1) of the Rating Valuations Act 1998" (identically for annual value and land value). s.27(4): "The database must include, in relation to each rating unit within the local authority's district,— (a) all information that relates to the unit that is included in the district valuation roll for the district". s.5 again: "district valuation roll means,— (a) in relation to a territorial authority, a roll prepared for a district under section 7 of the Rating Valuations Act 1998 and approved under section 11 of that Act". This is New Zealand's exact counterpart to NSW Local Government Act 1993 s.498's cross-Act citation of the Valuation of Land Act 1916.
tt: District valuation roll (general revaluation)

The Rules then set the content (rule 2.1), the sale-detail capture (rule 4.4.2: "The territorial authority must enter sale details in the DVR supporting information, as set out in rule 2.2, within 15 working days of receiving the necessary documentation") and the acceptance test (rule 5.5.1: "Where capital values or only land values are assessed, the proposed values, when compared to the market sales evidence, must satisfy the following statistical rules where appropriate: (a) coefficient of dispersion, which must be equal to or less than 12, (b) median value price ratio, which must be within the range 0.9 to 1.1, (c) price related differential which must be within the range 0.98 and 1.03, and (d) comparison of average value changes between sold and unsold properties, which must be equal to or less than 5 %.").

NOT trap 5a -- "To maintain consistency with ANZSIC" would be a comparability claim on its own, but the derivation sentence (built using ANZSIC's own principles, structure not broken) is a construction claim.

q: How Benefits are Adjusted Annual benefit rate changes are calculated using the standard escalator amount established in the Alberta Personal Income Tax Act, which is the lesser of either two per cent, or the Alberta Consumer Price Index (CPI) amount from October through September year-over-year.
b: The archived 2023-2025 version of the 'Indexing of Benefits' policy in the Alberta AISH policy manual (retained on the current Benefit Rate Adjustments page) states: 'AISH benefits are adjusted annually using the Alberta Consumer Price Index (CPI) starting on January 1, 2023 ... Annual benefit rate changes are calculated using the Alberta CPI (All-items, not seasonally adjusted). The Alberta CPI is published monthly by Statistics Canada and measures the change in price for goods and services bought by Albertans.' It sets out the formula X = A/B - 1, where A is the sum of the monthly Alberta CPI indexes for the 12 months ending September 30 before the adjustment date and B is the sum for the preceding 12 months. From January 1, 2026 the dependence on Alberta CPI is mediated by the Alberta escalator, which is capped at 2%.

q: the Consumer Price Index for Alberta for any 12-month period is the result arrived at by (a) aggregating the Consumer Price Index for Alberta, as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act (Canada) ... for each month in that period, (b) dividing the aggregate ... by 12
b: Alberta Personal Income Tax Act, RSA 2000 c A-30, s. 44.2(0.1)(b) defines the Alberta escalator, absent a prescribed percentage, as the lesser of 2% and the amount determined by the formula A/B - 1, 'where A is the Consumer Price Index for Alberta for the 12-month period that ended on the last September 30 before that year, and B is the Consumer Price Index for Alberta for the 12-month period immediately preceding'. Subsection 44.2(3) then defines that index explicitly: 'the Consumer Price Index for Alberta for any 12-month period is the result arrived at by (a) aggregating the Consumer Price Index for Alberta, as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act (Canada) ... for each month in that period, (b) dividing the aggregate ... by 12'.

Alberta Personal Income Tax Act, RSA 2000 c A-30, s. 44.2(2): 'Where the base taxation year ... in relation to a particular month is after 2024, each of the amounts expressed in dollars in section 30.2(2), except the amount of $2760, is to be adjusted so that the amount to be used under that subsection for the month is the total of (a) the amount that would, but for subsection (4), be the amount used under section 30.2(2) for the month that is one year before the particular month, and (b) the product obtained by multiplying (i) the amount referred to in clause (a) by (ii) the Alberta escalator for the taxation year following the base taxation year.' Section 30.2(2) is the Alberta Child and Family Benefit formula, containing the per-child base and working component amounts and the net income phase-out thresholds. The $2,760 working-income entry threshold is expressly excluded from indexation.
tt: Alberta Escalator (Alberta Personal Income Tax Act indexation factor)

q: the sum of (A) the single senior non-deductible income amount under section 8 for the benefit adjustment year, plus (B) an amount equal to the maximum annual amount, not including retroactive payments and not adjusted for deferral, of the monthly pension payable to a single senior under the Old Age Security Act (Canada) in the calendar year that ended before the commencement of the benefit adjustment year.
b: The Seniors Benefit Act (RSA 2000 c S-7) Schedule puts federal OAS and GIS amounts directly inside the Alberta formulas. Schedule s. 9(2)(b)(ii) sets the special needs component income test as 'the sum of (A) the single senior non-deductible income amount under section 8 for the benefit adjustment year, plus (B) an amount equal to the maximum annual amount, not including retroactive payments and not adjusted for deferral, of the monthly pension payable to a single senior under the Old Age Security Act (Canada) in the calendar year that ended before the commencement of the benefit adjustment year.' Schedule s. 7(4) defines term C of the supplementary accommodation assistance formula as 'the combined maximum annual amount ... of Old Age Security, not adjusted for deferral, and Guaranteed Income Supplement payable to a single senior and the maximum benefit payable to a single senior under section 4, in the previous calendar year.' The programme page corroborates that receipt of OAS is an eligibility condition and that lines 11300 (OAS) and 14600 (net federal supplements: GIS and Allowance) are deducted in arriving at non-deductible income (https://www.alberta.ca/alberta-seniors-benefit).

Seniors Benefit Act, RSA 2000 c S-7, s. 1(a.21): "'Alberta escalator' means the Alberta escalator as defined in section 44.2 of the Alberta Personal Income Tax Act". The Schedule, s. 2 ('Calculation of adjusted benefit amounts'), then provides: 'A benefit or an amount used to calculate a benefit or eligibility for a benefit that is to be adjusted under section 2.1(3)(b), (3.1)(b) or (5)(a)(ii) or 2.2(3)(b) or (5)(b) of this Act must be adjusted by an amount equal to (a) the benefit amount or amount as of December 31 of the previous calendar year, including any increase to that amount made under this Act or the regulations, multiplied by (b) the Alberta escalator.' So the Alberta Seniors Benefit annual cash benefit and the amounts used to calculate eligibility for it move with the same 2%-capped escalator as AISH, Income Support and the ACFB.
tt: Alberta Escalator (Alberta Personal Income Tax Act indexation factor)

q: 11(1) In this section, “Alberta CPI” means the monthly All-items Consumer Price Index for Alberta, not seasonally adjusted, published by Statistics Canada. (2) The maximum amount of the accommodation charge set by the Minister under section 9(4) of the Act in respect of each type of accommodation must be adjusted annually on August 1 by the lesser of the following: (a) the percentage increase in the Alberta CPI for the 12-month period ending on February 28 of that year, rounded to the nearest $0.05; (b) 3.8%.
b: RESOLVED 2026-08-09 (browser session, closing the item G.64.md left as cheap check 1). Continuing Care (Ministerial) Regulation, Alta Reg 44/2024 under the Continuing Care Act, SA 2022, c C-26.7 -- office consolidation with amendments up to and including AR 199/2025, current as of August 27, 2025, fetched in full via a Chrome browser session (a direct fetch-tool request to the same PDF URL returns ROBOTS_DISALLOWED; the King's Printer PDF itself carries no such restriction against ordinary browser access). Section 11 in full: '11(1) In this section, “Alberta CPI” means the monthly All-items Consumer Price Index for Alberta, not seasonally adjusted, published by Statistics Canada. (2) The maximum amount of the accommodation charge set by the Minister under section 9(4) of the Act in respect of each type of accommodation must be adjusted annually on August 1 by the lesser of the following: (a) the percentage increase in the Alberta CPI for the 12-month period ending on February 28 of that year, rounded to the nearest $0.05; (b) 3.8%.' This both settles the edge and explains the number on Alberta Health's programme page: the 1.8% increase stated to take effect August 1, 2026 is the CPI figure under (a), sitting below the 3.8% cap under (b) and so the binding term. Note the reference window is 12 months ending February 28, not September 30 as in the other Alberta-CPI edges in this slice -- this regulation runs its own, differently-dated formula.

q: if the Bank sets the policy interest rate at 2.25% ... the lower end of the range is 2.20%—our deposit rate; the higher end of the range is 2.5%—our bank rate.
b: Pure arithmetic on the target. The Bank's explainer works the example: 'if the Bank sets the policy interest rate at 2.25% ... the lower end of the range is 2.20%—our deposit rate; the higher end of the range is 2.5%—our bank rate.' The offsets are policy choices that change rarely — the deposit rate moved from equal to the target to 5 basis points below it in January 2025 — but between such changes the band is a fixed spread and nothing else.

q: by encouraging financial institutions to borrow and lend among themselves at close to the policy rate, the Bank affects interest rates on all kinds of other borrowing in the economy, including the prime rate of commercial banks (used for loans such as mortgages and lines of credit)
b: The Bank names this transmission directly: the policy rate 'is the starting point for setting many of the interest rates in the economy that matter for Canadians', and 'by encouraging financial institutions to borrow and lend among themselves at close to the policy rate, the Bank affects interest rates on all kinds of other borrowing in the economy, including the prime rate of commercial banks (used for loans such as mortgages and lines of credit)'. Deliberately not calculated_from: no bank is obliged to move prime, and the Bank's own word is 'affects'. The spread has been stable for years by convention, not by rule.

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, and the most valuable edge in this file because it runs from an EXISTING Russian node straight into the international layer with no new node required -- it is what connects Russia's CPI chain to the rest of the graph. Приказ Росстата № 915's Приложение № 1, п. 2 states its own derivation: «Методология подготовлена с учетом международных рекомендаций, изложенных в «Резолюции об индексах потребительских цен», принятой 17-ой Международной конференцией статистиков труда, и «Руководстве по индексу потребительских цен: Концепции и Методы»¹, разработанном Межсекретариатской рабочей группой по статистике цен (МРГСЦ), включая Евростат, Международной организацией труда (МОТ), Международным валютным фондом (МВФ), Организацией экономического сотрудничества и развития (ОЭСР), Европейской экономической комиссией Организации Объединенных Наций (ЕЭК ООН) и Всемирным банком.» THE EDITION IS PINNED IN FOOTNOTE 1, printed in English in the Russian original: «¹ Consumer price index manual: Concepts and Methods / 2020 / International Labour Organization/International Monetary Fund/Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development/Statistical Office of the European Union (Eurostat)/United Nations Economic Commission for Europe/The World Bank. https://www.imf.org/en/Data/Statistics/cpi-manual.» That is the 2020 edition, naming all six sponsoring organisations and the IMF-hosted URL, and it matches the `cpi-manual` node, whose own description identifies it as the 2020 edition updating the 2004 ILO-managed predecessor -- checked before minting, because had the node been the 2004 edition this edge would have had to be refused. WEAKNESS STATED: «с учетом» means "taking into account", which is softer than «в соответствии с» ("in accordance with"); this is an acknowledged-guidance dependency rather than a mandatory conformance claim. `methodology_depends_on` is still correct -- the manual supplies the method the Russian instrument is built on -- but the hedge is real and is recorded here rather than smoothed away.
tt: Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods
tp: IMF, ILO, OECD, Eurostat, UNECE and the World Bank

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, with the edition named unambiguously and repeatedly. The methodology's stated purpose is derivation from the standard: «Цель данной методологии – разработка алгоритма формирования показателей нефинансовых счетов сектора домашних хозяйств в системе национальных счетов Российской Федерации на основе Руководства «Система национальных счетов 2008»¹ (далее – СНС 2008).» The footnote gives a full bibliographic citation -- «¹ Система национальных счетов 2008: Пер. с англ. / Еврокомиссия, МВФ, ОЭСР, ООН, Всемирный банк. – Нью-Йорк, 2012.» -- and a terminology note confirms which edition's language is used: «При подготовке документа использована терминология, зафиксированная в русскоязычном издании СНС 2008 года, опубликованном Секретариатом ООН в 2012 году.» «СНС 2008» appears 44 times in the document. `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`: «на основе Руководства…» ("on the basis of the Manual") is a derivation claim in a legally approved official statistical methodology, not a background mention. SCOPE WEAKNESS, stated: this is a SECTORAL methodology (household non-financial accounts), so the edge is narrower than "Russian national accounts depend on SNA 2008" in general -- but at least five sibling Rosstat orders make the same citation for other parts of the accounts, several with a stronger conformance verb, and they are listed in `_dropped` so a future round can broaden the coverage without re-researching it.

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A. Rosstat states that its GDP release timetable is determined by the IMF standard: «Сроки представления данных по ВВП публикуются в «Федеральном плане статистических работ» и соответствуют срокам публикации этого показателя, определенным Специальным стандартом распространения данных МВФ, к которому присоединилась Россия 31 января 2005 года.» ("The release dates for GDP data … correspond to the publication deadlines for this indicator ESTABLISHED BY the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standard, to which Russia acceded on 31 January 2005.") NO EDITION PROBLEM: the SDDS is a single named standard rather than an edition series, the corpus holds one `imf-sdds` node, and the Russian text names it in full («Специальный стандарт распространения данных МВФ») and pins the accession date. `methodology_depends_on` because the dependency is real and operative, with the scope stated honestly: it is a dependency on the SDDS's TIMELINESS dimension -- what must be published when -- not on GDP concepts, which come from the SNA. Independently corroborated from a different institution's document: the Bank of Russia's own SDDS page states that the same requirements cover «Данные Росстат».
tt: IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS)

b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, and the most explicit methodological-dependency statement found in the Russian branch. The dependency governs presentation as well as concepts -- «Основные агрегаты представляют собой набор главных компонентов платежного баланса, рекомендованных в РПБ6…» and «Интерпретация знаков платежного баланса (согласно РПБ6)». EDITION NAMED unambiguously as «шестое издание» plus the abbreviation РПБ6, matching `imf-bpm6` exactly; two Bank of Russia SDDS metadata sheets corroborate with the publication YEAR as well, e.g. «…шестое издание «Руководства по платежному балансу и международной инвестиционной позиции» (РПБ6) Международного Валютного Фонда, 2009…». b: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, and structurally the strongest dependency in the Russian branch even though it is typed conservatively. The SDDS appears in the ENABLING PREAMBLE of a numbered, Minjust-registered Minfin order -- part of the legal authority under which the government-finance-statistics procedure is issued, not a methodological reference: «…постановления Правительства Российской Федерации от 26 сентября 1997 г. № 1226 "О присоединении Российской Федерации к Специальному стандарту распространения данных МВФ" …, в целях совершенствования методологии формирования информации по статистике государственных финансов п р и к а з ы в а ю:». The standard's full Russian name appears verbatim in the order's own text, so the requirement that the dependent document name the standard itself is satisfied, even though the immediate instrument cited is the 1997 Government Resolution effecting accession. `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on` DELIBERATELY: the SDDS here supplies legal authority and a transmission obligation (the Порядок §22 requires Treasury transmission «в Международный валютный фонд» on a fixed timetable), while the compilation METHOD the order actually prescribes is described only by unversioned reference to «руководствами по распространению (раскрытию) данных» -- so a methodology-typed edge would overstate what this document says. A TENSE/EVENT NOTE worth preserving: Постановление № 1226 is dated 1997 while Rosstat's GDP procedure gives Russia's SDDS accession as 31 January 2005. These are two different events -- the 1997 resolution authorises accession, 2005 is the subscription date -- and they are not contradictory.
tt: IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS)

Representative row, NAICS 3111 Animal food manufacturing, under 'Gross output': 'Sales and inventory change in constant prices, Monthly Survey of Manufacturing, Record no (number). 2101. Industrial product price indexes, Record no (number). 2318.' Record 2318 is the IPPI. `uses_data_from` follows the type already taken for statcan-gdp-monthly -> statcan-cpi, which rests on the identical evidence in the identical document. WORTH STATING PLAINLY: this is the best-evidenced deflator edge in the Canadian corpus and it was the last one built. The same table names the CPI in 27 rows and SEPH in 37, and both of those became edges two sessions before this one — the IPPI was invisible only because nobody had grepped for it. q: The main data source of deflators for manufactured goods is the Industrial Product Price Indexes (IPPI) produced by Statistics Canada's Prices Division. Prior to 1981, deflators were based on Industry Selling Price Indexes (ISPI).
b: Catalogue 15F0077GIE, 'A Guide to Deflating the Input-Output Accounts: Sources and Methods' (2001), which record 1301 cites as the description of the double-deflation method used to produce constant-price GDP by industry. Under the heading 'Sources of deflators', unhedged: 'The main data source of deflators for manufactured goods is the Industrial Product Price Indexes (IPPI) produced by Statistics Canada's Prices Division. Prior to 1981, deflators were based on Industry Selling Price Indexes (ISPI).' Earlier in the same chapter, on why basic-price deflation is possible where purchaser-price deflation is not: 'the commodity price information collected by the Prices Division to compile industry product price indexes can be used to construct deflators for values at basic prices. These Industrial Product Price Indexes (IPPI), aggregated where necessary to the input-output classification, constitute the main source of deflators for manufactured commodities.' Both passages verified verbatim against the PDF. `methodology_depends_on` matches the type taken for statcan-sut -> statcan-cpi from the same document. ONE HEDGE, STATED, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE: the guide is a 2001 edition marked ARCHIVED, twenty-five years old, and it remains the document record 1301 points at for this method. The 'can be used' softness that qualifies the CPI edge does not apply here — the 'Sources of deflators' sentence says 'is'.
tt: Industrial Product Price Index (IPPI)

Record 2318, under Estimation: 'For the IPPI, commodity and industry weights are derived from a combination of the 2019 Supply and Use Tables that closely reflect actual economic transactions by industry and the sales of goods manufactured by companies as reported for the 2019 ASML.' The same section adds that the industry indexes are 'aggregated to the level required for the input-output tables and the measurement of Gross Domestic Product', so the tables set the aggregation structure as well as the weights. Admissible under the V0.10 mutual-partner rule on its own terms: each direction is stated by a different document in its own words, each carries its own evidence_url, and the two are asymmetric in kind rather than restatements of one relationship — the tables take the IPPI as a price measure, the IPPI takes the tables as a weighting frame. `relationship_type` records the asymmetry as the rule requires: `methodology_depends_on` outbound from the tables against `uses_data_from` here, because the SUT figures are a direct numerical input to the weights rather than a method the IPPI follows. THE MECHANISM IS NOT SIMULTANEOUS AND THAT MATTERS FOR READING THE CYCLE: the 2019 tables weight today's index, and today's index deflates a later vintage of the tables. Nothing circular happens in any single calculation; the loop closes only across vintages, five years apart.

q: The total trade margin at constant prices is calculated as the difference between the purchaser value, deflated with the appropriate Consumer Price Index (CPI), and the sum of the basic value and the ...
b: Catalogue 15F0077GIE, 'A Guide to Deflating the Input-Output Accounts: Sources and Methods' (2001), which record 1301 cites as the description of the double-deflation method used to produce constant-price GDP by industry. Chapter 2, in the passage on trade margins: 'Consumer price indexes can be used to deflate the purchaser value of commodities sold for personal expenditure. Similarly, industry product price indexes are used to deflate the basic values of the same commodities. This has made it possible to calculate the trade margin for commodities bought for personal expenditure as a residual using both of these observed prices.' `methodology_depends_on` rather than `uses_data_from` because this document is the accounts' deflation methodology and the index is named as the price measure the method takes, which is the case the type comment describes. ONE HEDGE REMAINS, AND ONE WAS RETIRED IN V0.11. Retired: the 'can be used' softness above is not the document's last word on the CPI. Four sentences later in the same passage, unhedged and read while verifying the IPPI quotations, the guide states the mechanism outright: 'The total trade margin at constant prices is calculated as the difference between the purchaser value, deflated with the appropriate Consumer Price Index (CPI), and the sum of the basic value and the ...'. 'Deflated with' is a statement of what deflates what, which is exactly what the hedged sentence was recorded as lacking, so this edge is stronger than V0.10 believed and was under-rated by a first reading that stopped at the first mention. Still standing: the guide is a 2001 edition marked ARCHIVED — it remains the document record 1301 points at for this method, but it is twenty-five years old and a later methodology note may supersede it.

q: The input-output framework is validated for accuracy, coherence and overall reasonableness. The major components of the framework, such as the income and expenditure-based GDP components are reconciled to the national and provincial-territorial income and expenditure accounts.
b: The reverse of statcan-national-accounts -> statcan-sut, and taken deliberately under the V0.10 decision that a node may be a mutual definitional partner. Record 1401, Quality evaluation: 'The input-output framework is validated for accuracy, coherence and overall reasonableness. The major components of the framework, such as the income and expenditure-based GDP components are reconciled to the national and provincial-territorial income and expenditure accounts.' Record 1901 states the converse in its own Estimation section: 'The annual benchmarks for GDP by the income approach and by the expenditure approach are generated through the construction of annual supply and use tables which balance the supply of each product in the economy against its use.' Neither statement is a mistake and neither supersedes the other — annual benchmarking is an iterative balancing process in which each side constrains the other, which is what the accounts mean by coherence. The pair is asymmetric in strength and the `relationship_type` records that: 1901 discloses the SUT as the source of its benchmark levels (`calculated_from`), while 1401 describes reconciliation as a validation step rather than an input (`methodology_depends_on`), so the cycle is not symmetric in weight and does not assert that the two are interchangeable.

q: on July 1, 2020, and every July 1 thereafter, the board shall adjust the taxes imposed by subdivisions (a), (b), and (c) ... by increasing the taxes by a percentage amount equal to the increase in the California Consumer Price Index, as calculated by the Department of Finance with the resulting taxe
b: Revenue and Taxation Code §7360(d), added by SB 1 in 2017, provides that "on July 1, 2020, and every July 1 thereafter, the board shall adjust the taxes imposed by subdivisions (a), (b), and (c) ... by increasing the taxes by a percentage amount equal to the increase in the California Consumer Price Index, as calculated by the Department of Finance with the resulting taxes rounded to the nearest one-tenth of one cent." CDTFA's own notice repeats the requirement. Recorded ambiguity: the statute attributes calculation of the California CPI to the Department of Finance, whereas the index is in fact produced by the Department of Industrial Relations, and neither the statute nor the CDTFA notices reconcile this.
tt: California Consumer Price Index
tp: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Labor Statistics and Research

The Franchise Tax Board confirms the practice, reporting a 3.0 percent factor from June 2024 to June 2025 applied to brackets, filing thresholds, the standard deduction, exemption credits and the renter's credit limits.
tt: California Consumer Price Index
tp: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Labor Statistics and Research

q: The Social Security Act specifies a formula for determining each COLA. According to the formula, COLAs are based on increases in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). CPI-Ws are calculated on a monthly basis by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. A COLA effective for December of the current year is equal to the percentage increase (if any) in the CPI-W from the average for the third quarter of the current year to the average for the third quarter of the last year in which a COLA became effective.
b: SSA states the statutory formula outright: 'The Social Security Act specifies a formula for determining each COLA. According to the formula, COLAs are based on increases in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). CPI-Ws are calculated on a monthly basis by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. A COLA effective for December of the current year is equal to the percentage increase (if any) in the CPI-W from the average for the third quarter of the current year to the average for the third quarter of the last year in which a COLA became effective.' The arithmetic is shown in full: the 2.8 percent COLA effective December 2025 is (317.265 - 308.729) / 308.729 x 100, using the July, August and September CPI-W values for 2024 and 2025. Note the index is CPI-W, a subpopulation index for urban wage earners and clerical workers, not the headline CPI-U.

q: We use the average wage indexing series to update several amounts that are important to the operation of Social Security's Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (OASDI) program. — OASDI contribution and benefit base (also known as the taxable maximum); Retirement earnings test exempt amounts; Formulas for a primary insurance amount and maximum family benefits; Amount of earnings needed to earn a quarter of coverage.
b: SSA lists the amounts driven by the wage index and puts the taxable maximum first: 'We use the average wage indexing series to update several amounts that are important to the operation of Social Security's Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (OASDI) program. — OASDI contribution and benefit base (also known as the taxable maximum); Retirement earnings test exempt amounts; Formulas for a primary insurance amount and maximum family benefits; Amount of earnings needed to earn a quarter of coverage.' This is the interesting structural fact about the Social Security system: benefits are indexed to prices, the tax base is indexed to wages, and the two indices diverge.
tt: National Average Wage Index (AWI)
tp: US Social Security Administration, Office of the Chief Actuary

q: Population controls are independent estimates of the population that are used to weight the CPS sample results so that estimates reflect the civilian noninstitutional population ages 16 and older. The Census Bureau develops the CPS population controls, which are based on decennial census population counts, supplemented with birth and death data and estimates of net international migration. The Census Bureau reviews and adjusts the population estimates every year. BLS introduces the Census Bureau's annual population control adjustments into CPS estimates for January.
b: The Handbook of Methods is unambiguous that the survey cannot produce population levels by itself: 'Population controls are independent estimates of the population that are used to weight the CPS sample results so that estimates reflect the civilian noninstitutional population ages 16 and older. The Census Bureau develops the CPS population controls, which are based on decennial census population counts, supplemented with birth and death data and estimates of net international migration. The Census Bureau reviews and adjusts the population estimates every year. BLS introduces the Census Bureau's annual population control adjustments into CPS estimates for January.' This is why the January Employment Situation carries a break in the household series each year — the level jumps by whatever the new vintage says, independent of anything that happened in the labour market.
tt: Population Estimates Program (Vintage Estimates)

q: based on decennial census population counts, supplemented with birth and death data and estimates of net international migration
b: The population controls are 'based on decennial census population counts, supplemented with birth and death data and estimates of net international migration' — the estimates programme is a carry-forward of the decennial base, which is why a census undercount or overcount propagates into every intercensal year until the next census resets it.
tt: Decennial Census of Population and Housing

q: When the Census Bureau's processing activities are completed, the microdata file is securely transferred to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) for estimation of labor force statistics.
b: The Employment Situation news release is two surveys stapled together. The household half — the unemployment rate, the participation rate, and all demographic detail — is the CPS. BLS: 'When the Census Bureau's processing activities are completed, the microdata file is securely transferred to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) for estimation of labor force statistics.' The establishment half (payroll employment) is the CES, already linked to QCEW elsewhere in the graph.
tt: Current Population Survey (CPS)
tp: US Census Bureau and US Bureau of Labor Statistics

q: As required by law, this update is accomplished by increasing the latest published Census Bureau poverty thresholds by the applicable percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U).
b: The statute names the index: 'Section 673(2) of the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (OBRA) of 1981 (42 U.S.C. 9902(2)) requires the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services to update the poverty guidelines at least annually, adjusting them on the basis of the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U). ... As required by law, this update is accomplished by increasing the latest published Census Bureau poverty thresholds by the applicable percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U). The guidelines in this 2026 notice reflect the 2.63 percent price increase between calendar years 2024 and 2025.' Note this is CPI-U, annual average to annual average — a different index and a different reference period from the CPI-W third-quarter comparison that drives the Social Security COLA.

q: As required by law, this update is accomplished by increasing the latest published Census Bureau poverty thresholds by the applicable percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U).
b: The guidelines are not an independent measure — they are the Census thresholds inflated and smoothed: 'The poverty guidelines issued here are a simplified version of the poverty thresholds that the Census Bureau uses to prepare its estimates of the number of individuals and families in poverty. ... this update is accomplished by increasing the latest published Census Bureau poverty thresholds by the applicable percentage change in the CPI-U. ... The poverty guidelines continue to be derived from the Census Bureau's current official poverty thresholds; they are not derived from the Census Bureau's Supplemental Poverty Measure (SPM).' The notice even states the guidelines are 'roughly equal to the poverty thresholds for calendar year 2025, which the Census Bureau expects to publish in final form in September 2026' — the administrative number arrives eight months before the statistical number it approximates.
tt: Census Bureau Poverty Thresholds (Income and Poverty in the United States)

b: The Census Bureau's own methodology page labels the published threshold table 'Poverty Thresholds by Size of Family and Number of Related Children Under 18 Years — Source: Current Population Survey (CPS)'. The threshold matrix is carried forward by CPI-U, but the income distribution it is applied to, and the official count of people in poverty, come from the CPS Annual Social and Economic Supplement.
tt: Current Population Survey (CPS)
tp: US Census Bureau and US Bureau of Labor Statistics

q: The official poverty thresholds do not vary geographically, but they are updated for inflation using the Consumer Price Index (CPI-U)... Thresholds are updated annually for inflation using the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U).
b: 'The official poverty thresholds do not vary geographically, but they are updated for inflation using the Consumer Price Index (CPI-U)... Thresholds are updated annually for inflation using the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U).' Worth noting the doubling-up: the thresholds are CPI-indexed, and then HHS indexes the published thresholds forward by CPI again to get the guidelines, so the CPI enters the eligibility rule for Medicaid twice, a year apart.

q: (3)(A) The cost-of-living adjustment for any calendar year is the percentage (if any) by which (i) the C-CPI-U for the preceding calendar year, exceeds (ii) the CPI for calendar year 2016, multiplied by the amount determined under subparagraph (B).
b: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 says the figures 'are generally determined by reference to § 1(f)', and 26 U.S.C. § 1(f) names the index and the reference period exactly: '(3)(A) The cost-of-living adjustment for any calendar year is the percentage (if any) by which (i) the C-CPI-U for the preceding calendar year, exceeds (ii) the CPI for calendar year 2016, multiplied by the amount determined under subparagraph (B).' '(6)(A) The term "C-CPI-U" means the Chained Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics of the Department of Labor). The values ... shall be the latest values so published as of the date on which such Bureau publishes the initial value of the Chained Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers for the month of August for the preceding calendar year.' '(6)(B) The C-CPI-U for any calendar year is the average of the C-CPI-U as of the close of the 12-month period ending on August 31 of such calendar year.' The August cut-off is why the IRS can publish next year's brackets in October, and the freeze on 'latest values as of' the initial August release is how the statute copes with the fact that the chained index is revised for a year after first publication.
tt: Chained Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (C-CPI-U)

q: all three of the CPI indexes are built in two stages. In the first stage, prices for each of the 7,776 item-area combinations (243 item categories X 32 geographic areas) are averaged together to form 7,776 basic indexes... The geometric mean estimator is used in the C-CPI-U in the same item categories in which it is used in the CPI-U and CPI-W. In the second stage... It is at this second stage where the C-CPI-U is different from the CPI-U and CPI-W. The use of a superlative formula for upper-level aggregation... is designed to address consumer substitution across item categories.
b: The chained index is not a separate collection — it is the CPI's own price quotes reaggregated. BLS: 'all three of the CPI indexes are built in two stages. In the first stage, prices for each of the 7,776 item-area combinations (243 item categories X 32 geographic areas) are averaged together to form 7,776 basic indexes... The geometric mean estimator is used in the C-CPI-U in the same item categories in which it is used in the CPI-U and CPI-W. In the second stage... It is at this second stage where the C-CPI-U is different from the CPI-U and CPI-W. The use of a superlative formula for upper-level aggregation... is designed to address consumer substitution across item categories.' BLS also confirms the policy use: 'Since 2017, the C-CPI-U has been used to adjust Federal tax brackets for inflation.' The average gap is about 0.2 percentage points a year, which compounds.

q: The estimates of quantities purchased, or real spending, for most of the detailed PCE categories are prepared by deflation. In this method, the quantities are calculated by dividing the current-dollar value of the component by an appropriate price index... For most PCE categories, the closest matching price index is a consumer price index or indexes.
b: NIPA Handbook Chapter 5 lists the CPI among the principal inputs — 'The following are among the principal source data used for the PCE estimates: BEA's Benchmark Input-Output (I-O) Accounts... the Census Bureau's Annual Retail Trade Survey, Service Annual Survey, Quarterly Services Survey, and Monthly Retail Trade Survey; and the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Consumer Price Indexes (CPIs)' — and then explains the mechanism: 'The estimates of quantities purchased, or real spending, for most of the detailed PCE categories are prepared by deflation. In this method, the quantities are calculated by dividing the current-dollar value of the component by an appropriate price index... For most PCE categories, the closest matching price index is a consumer price index or indexes.' Tables 5.A and 5.B name the specific CPI series component by component (CPI for new cars, CPI for used cars and trucks, CPI for food at home, and so on). The Fed's preferred inflation gauge is therefore largely a reweighting of BLS price quotes onto national-accounts expenditure weights.

q: The Committee reaffirms its judgment that inflation at the rate of 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures, is most consistent over the longer run with the Federal Reserve's statutory maximum employment and price stability mandates.
b: The FOMC's Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy, reaffirmed effective January 27, 2026, names the series that defines the target: 'The Committee reaffirms its judgment that inflation at the rate of 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures, is most consistent over the longer run with the Federal Reserve's statutory maximum employment and price stability mandates.' The 2 percent goal is not defined on the CPI — a distinction that matters because the two indexes routinely differ by several tenths.

q: 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures
b: The Summary of Economic Projections reports each participant's projection of inflation as the percent change in the PCE price index and in the core PCE price index, precisely because the FOMC's longer-run goal is stated as '2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures'. The projection variable is defined by the statement of goals, so the SEP inherits BEA's index by construction.

q: the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW) universe employment series
b: The CES sampling frame 'is built from unemployment insurance (UI) quarterly tax records', and the net birth–death model that fills the gap left by firms too new to sample is derived from 'the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW) universe employment series' via an ARIMA projection on ten years of QCEW history. b: The BLS Handbook of Methods CPI data sources chapter states that price information for used cars and trucks is obtained from J.D. Power Valuation Services, and that new vehicle price data comes from J.D. Power transaction data, rather than from the CPI's own outlet sample. Promoted from _dropped in V0.5 under the commercial-source decision.
